units.zh: 韓子曰：「儒以文亂法，而俠以武犯禁。」
units.en: Han Feizi once wrote: "Confucian scholars subvert the law with their writings, and wandering knights defy authority with their swords."
units.literal: Han Feizi said: "The Confucians use their writings to undermine the law, while the knights-errant use their martial prowess to violate the prohibitions."

units.zh: 二者皆譏，而學士多稱於世云。
units.en: Both were censured, yet scholars have always found admirers in the world.
units.literal: Both of these are criticized, yet scholars are much praised by the world.

units.zh: 至如以術取宰相卿大夫，輔翼其世主，功名俱著於春秋，固無可言者。
units.en: Those who rose to become chancellors and ministers through political craft, who served as their lord's right hand, whose deeds and reputations fill the histories — they need no further comment.
units.literal: As for those who by craft attained the positions of chancellor, ministers, and grandees, who assisted and supported their rulers, their achievements and fame all recorded in the annals, there is nothing that needs to be said about them.

units.zh: 及若季次、原憲，閭巷人也，讀書懷獨行君子之德，義不茍合當世，當世亦笑之。
units.en: Then there were men like Ji Ci and Yuan Xian — common folk of the lanes and alleys who cherished their books and upheld the solitary virtues of the true gentleman. They refused on principle to bend to the age, and the age laughed at them in return.
units.literal: As for Ji Ci and Yuan Xian, they were men of the back alleys, who read books and held fast to the virtues of the solitary-minded gentleman, whose integrity refused to compromise with their times, and their times also laughed at them.

units.zh: 故季次、原憲終身空室蓬戶，褐衣疏食不厭。
units.en: So Ji Ci and Yuan Xian lived out their days in bare rooms behind wattle doors, clad in rough cloth and eating thin gruel, yet never once complained.
units.literal: Thus, Ji Ci and Yuan Xian lived their whole lives in empty rooms with bramble-woven doors, in coarse garments and meager food without complaint.

units.zh: 死而已四百餘年，而弟子志之不倦。
units.en: More than four hundred years after their deaths, their disciples still honor their memory without flagging.
units.literal: They have been dead for over four hundred years, yet their disciples record them without tiring.

units.zh: 今游俠，其行雖不軌於正義，然其言必信，其行必果，已諾必誠，不愛其軀，赴士之阸困，既已存亡死生矣，而不矜其能，羞伐其德，蓋亦有足多者焉。
units.en: Now consider the wandering knights. Their conduct may not conform to orthodox morality, yet when they give their word they keep it, when they commit to action they see it through, and when they make a promise they honor it with their lives. They throw themselves into the perils of others without sparing their own bodies, having stared down life and death without flinching — and yet they never boast of their abilities or trumpet their virtue. Surely there is much in them to admire.
units.literal: Now the wandering knights, though their conduct may not conform to standards of righteousness, yet their words are always trustworthy, their actions always decisive, their promises always kept; they do not spare their own bodies, they rush to the aid of gentlemen in distress, having already risked life and death, yet they do not boast of their abilities, are ashamed to brag of their virtues — there is indeed much in them worthy of praise.

units.zh: 且緩急，人之所時有也。
units.en: After all, desperate need is something that comes to every person sooner or later.
units.literal: Moreover, the need for urgent help is something that comes to everyone from time to time.

units.zh: 太史公曰：昔者虞舜窘於井廩，伊尹負於鼎俎，傅說匿於傅險，呂尚困於棘津，夷吾桎梏，百里飯牛，仲尼畏匡，菜色陳、蔡。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: In the old days, Emperor Shun was nearly killed in a well and a granary. Yi Yin labored among the pots and cutting boards. Fu Yue hid himself at the cliffs of Fu. Lu Shang was reduced to desperate straits at Jijin. Guan Zhong wore fetters. Baili Xi fed cattle for a living. Confucius was besieged at Kuang and went hungry until his face turned sallow between Chen and Cai.
units.literal: The Grand Historian said: In ancient times, Emperor Shun was trapped in a well and a granary; Yi Yin bore the burdens of the cooking vessels; Fu Yue hid at the cliff of Fu; Lu Shang was stranded at Jijin; Guan Zhong wore fetters; Baili Xi herded cattle; Confucius was threatened at Kuang, and his face grew gaunt at Chen and Cai.

units.zh: 此皆學士所謂有道仁人也，猶然遭此菑，況以中材而涉亂世之末流乎？
units.en: All of these were the very paragons that scholars call men of virtue and benevolence — yet even they suffered such calamities. How much worse, then, for ordinary people struggling through the dregs of a disordered age?
units.literal: These were all what scholars call men of the Way and benevolence, yet they still suffered such calamities — how much more so for those of ordinary talent who wade through the turbid currents of a disordered age?

units.zh: 其遇害何可勝道哉！
units.en: The calamities such men suffer are beyond all telling!
units.literal: The harm they encountered — how can it be fully described!

units.zh: 鄙人有言曰：「何知仁義，已饗其利者為有德。」
units.en: Common folk have a saying: "What does anyone know about benevolence and righteousness? Whoever reaps the profits is the one called virtuous."
units.literal: The common people have a saying: "What do they know of benevolence and righteousness? Those who have enjoyed the benefits are considered virtuous."

units.zh: 故伯夷丑周，餓死首陽山，而文武不以其故貶王；
units.en: Bo Yi despised the Zhou conquest and starved himself to death on Mount Shouyang, yet Kings Wen and Wu were nonetheless regarded as kings on that account.
units.literal: Thus, Bo Yi despised the Zhou dynasty and starved to death on Mount Shouyang, yet Kings Wen and Wu were not diminished in their kingship on his account;

units.zh: 跖、蹻暴戾，其徒誦義無窮。
units.en: Robber Zhi and Zhuang Qiao were violent and cruel, yet their followers sang praises to their righteousness without end.
units.literal: Zhi and Qiao were cruel and violent, yet their followers praised their righteousness without end.

units.zh: 由此觀之，「竊鉤者誅，竊國者侯，侯之門仁義存」，非虛言也。
units.en: Seen in this light, the old saying is no empty proverb: "Steal a belt buckle, and you are executed; steal a kingdom, and you are made a lord; at the lord's gate, the virtues of benevolence and righteousness take up residence."
units.literal: Looking at it from this perspective, "He who steals a belt buckle is executed, he who steals a kingdom becomes a feudal lord, and at the lord's gate benevolence and righteousness dwell" — these are not empty words.

units.zh: 今拘學或抱咫尺之義，久孤於世，豈若卑論儕俗，與世沈浮而取榮名哉！
units.en: Today's pedantic scholars may cling to their narrow slice of righteousness and remain alone in the world for a lifetime — but can that compare with those who lower their standards to the common level and ride the currents of the age to win glory and renown?
units.literal: Now those confined scholars who cling to their narrow righteousness, long isolated from the world — how can they compare with those who lower their discourse to match the vulgar, who rise and fall with the world to win glory and fame!

units.zh: 而布衣之徒，設取予然諾，千里誦義，為死不顧世，此亦有所長，非茍而已也。
units.en: Yet among the common people there are those whose dealings are governed by honor, whose word is celebrated a thousand li away, who face death without a second thought for worldly consequence — there is something admirable in this that should not be dismissed.
units.literal: Yet common men who set their giving and receiving, their promises and pledges, whose righteousness is praised a thousand li away, who face death without caring for worldly concerns — this too has its merits, it is not something trivial.

units.zh: 故士窮窘而得委命，此豈非人之所謂賢豪閒者邪？
units.en: When a gentleman is cornered and desperate and finds someone willing to stake their life on his behalf — is this not the very thing people mean when they speak of a worthy hero?
units.literal: Thus, when a gentleman finds himself in desperate straits and can entrust his life to another, is this not what people call a worthy and heroic person?

units.zh: 誠使鄉曲之俠，予季次、原憲比權量力，效功於當世，不同日而論矣。
units.en: If one were to weigh the local knights against Ji Ci and Yuan Xian in terms of power and achievement, measuring their service to the age — they simply cannot be spoken of in the same breath.
units.literal: If one truly compared the local knights-errant with Ji Ci and Yuan Xian in terms of power and ability, and measured their contributions to the world, they could not be spoken of in the same breath.

units.zh: 要以功見言信，俠客之義又曷可少哉！
units.en: In the end, when we judge by deeds accomplished and promises kept, how can anyone dismiss the code of the wandering knights?
units.literal: In sum, judging by their deeds and the trustworthiness of their words, how can the righteousness of the knights-errant be considered negligible!

units.zh: 古布衣之俠，靡得而聞已。
units.en: Of the ancient knights-errant who rose from the common people, nothing survives to tell their tales.
units.literal: The knights-errant of ancient times among the common people — none of them can be heard of anymore.

units.zh: 近世延陵、孟嘗、春申、平原、信陵之徒，皆因王者親屬，藉於有土卿相之富厚，招天下賢者，顯名諸侯，不可謂不賢者矣。
units.en: In more recent times, the Lord of Yanling, Lord Mengchang, Lord Chunshen, Lord Pingyuan, and Lord Xinling all drew on royal kinship and the vast wealth of their fiefs to attract the worthiest men under heaven and win renown among the feudal lords — they were, by any measure, men of worth.
units.literal: In recent times, the likes of Yanling, Lord Mengchang, Lord Chunshen, Lord Pingyuan, and Lord Xinling, all relied on their kinship with royalty and drew upon the wealth and resources of their fiefs and ministerial positions to attract the worthy men of the world, making their names illustrious among the feudal lords — they cannot be called anything but worthy men.

units.zh: 比如順風而呼，聲非加疾，其埶激也。
units.en: It is like shouting downwind — the voice itself is no louder, but the force of circumstance carries it far.
units.literal: It is like shouting with the wind at one's back — the voice is not louder, but the force of circumstance carries it further.

units.zh: 至如閭巷之俠，修行砥名，聲施於天下，莫不稱賢，是為難耳。
units.en: But the knights of the lanes and alleys who cultivated their conduct and burnished their reputations until their fame spread across the realm and all people praised them as worthy — that is the truly difficult thing.
units.literal: But as for the knights-errant of the lanes and alleys, who cultivated their conduct and polished their reputations, whose fame spread throughout the world, whom all praised as worthy — that is truly difficult.

units.zh: 然儒、墨皆排擯不載。
units.en: Yet both the Confucian and the Mohist schools rejected and excluded them, leaving them unrecorded.
units.literal: Yet both the Confucians and the Mohists rejected and excluded them, and did not record them.

units.zh: 自秦以前，匹夫之俠，湮滅不見，余甚恨之。
units.en: Before the Qin dynasty, the knights-errant who rose from humble origins were lost to oblivion. I find this deeply regrettable.
units.literal: Before the Qin dynasty, the knights-errant among the common men were buried and lost from sight — I deeply regret this.

units.zh: 以余所聞，漢興有朱家、田仲、王公、劇孟、郭解之徒，雖時捍當世之文罔，然其私義廉絜退讓，有足稱者。
units.en: From what I have heard, since the founding of the Han there have been men like Zhu Jia, Tian Zhong, Wang Gong, Ju Meng, and Guo Jie. Though they sometimes clashed with the laws of their day, their personal honor, integrity, and modesty were deserving of the highest praise.
units.literal: From what I have heard, since the rise of the Han there have been the likes of Zhu Jia, Tian Zhong, Wang Gong, Ju Meng, and Guo Jie, who though they sometimes ran afoul of the laws and prohibitions of the age, yet in their private righteousness, integrity, and modesty had much to commend them.

units.zh: 名不虛立，士不虛附。
units.en: Their reputations were not built on nothing, and the men who rallied to them did not do so without reason.
units.literal: Their reputations were not established in vain, and the gentlemen who followed them did not do so for nothing.

units.zh: 至如朋黨宗彊比周，設財役貧，豪暴侵淩孤弱，恣欲自快，游俠亦丑之。
units.en: As for those who formed factions and built up their clans through collusion, who used their wealth to exploit the poor, who bullied the helpless and the weak, who indulged their desires for their own pleasure — the wandering knights despised such people as much as anyone.
units.literal: As for those who formed cliques and strengthened their clans through collusion, who used their wealth to enslave the poor, who as powerful bullies oppressed the orphaned and weak, who indulged their desires to please themselves — the wandering knights despised them too.

units.zh: 余悲世俗不察其意，而猥以朱家、郭解等令與暴豪之徒同類而共笑之也。
units.en: It grieves me that the world fails to understand their true motives and carelessly lumps men like Zhu Jia and Guo Jie together with violent strongmen, deriding them all as one.
units.literal: I lament that common opinion fails to examine their true intent, and carelessly lumps men like Zhu Jia and Guo Jie together with the violent and powerful, and laughs at them all alike.

units.zh: 魯朱家者，與高祖同時。
units.en: Zhu Jia of Lu lived in the same era as Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Zhu Jia of Lu was a contemporary of Emperor Gaozu.

units.zh: 魯人皆以儒教，而朱家用俠聞。
units.en: The people of Lu were all devoted to Confucian learning, but Zhu Jia won his fame through knight-errantry.
units.literal: The people of Lu all followed Confucian teachings, yet Zhu Jia was known for his chivalry.

units.zh: 所藏活豪士以百數，其餘庸人不可勝言。
units.en: The fugitives and heroes he sheltered and saved numbered in the hundreds; the ordinary folk he helped were too many to count.
units.literal: The heroes he sheltered and saved numbered in the hundreds, and the ordinary people beyond that were too many to count.

units.zh: 然終不伐其能，歆其德，諸所嘗施，唯恐見之。
units.en: Yet he never boasted of his abilities or took pride in his virtuous deeds, and of all the people he had once helped, he dreaded nothing more than running into them again.
units.literal: Yet he never boasted of his abilities or gloried in his virtue; as for those he had once helped, he feared nothing more than to encounter them again.

units.zh: 振人不贍，先從貧賤始。
units.en: When he gave aid to those in need, he always started with the poorest and most humble.
units.literal: When he aided people in need, he always began with the poorest and most humble.

units.zh: 家無餘財，衣不完采，食不重味，乘不過軥牛。
units.en: His household had no spare wealth. His clothes bore no fine colors. His meals had no second course. His only conveyance was an ox-drawn cart.
units.literal: His household had no surplus wealth, his clothes were not finely colored, his meals had no second dish, and his conveyance was no more than a yoked ox.

units.zh: 專趨人之急，甚己之私。
units.en: He devoted himself entirely to the urgent needs of others, putting them above his own private concerns.
units.literal: He devoted himself wholly to the urgent needs of others, more than to his own private affairs.

units.zh: 既陰脫季布將軍之阸，及布尊貴，終身不見也。
units.en: After he had secretly rescued General Ji Bu from peril, once Ji Bu rose to a position of honor, Zhu Jia never sought him out again for the rest of his life.
units.literal: After he had secretly rescued General Ji Bu from danger, once Ji Bu rose to honor and eminence, Zhu Jia never saw him again for the rest of his life.

units.zh: 自關以東，莫不延頸願交焉。
units.en: From the Pass eastward, there was no one who did not crane their neck, hoping for the chance to befriend him.
units.literal: From the Pass eastward, there was no one who did not crane their necks and desire to form a friendship with him.

units.zh: 楚田仲以俠聞，喜劍，父事朱家，自以為行弗及。
units.en: Tian Zhong of Chu was known for his chivalry and loved swordsmanship. He served Zhu Jia with the respect due a father and considered his own conduct inferior to the master's.
units.literal: Tian Zhong of Chu was known for his chivalry, loved the sword, served Zhu Jia as a father, and considered his own conduct inferior.

units.zh: 田仲已死，而雒陽有劇孟。
units.en: After Tian Zhong passed away, there arose in Luoyang a man named Ju Meng.
units.literal: After Tian Zhong died, there was Ju Meng in Luoyang.

units.zh: 周人以商賈為資，而劇孟以任俠顯諸侯。
units.en: The people of the Zhou region made their living by trade, but Ju Meng won his fame among the lords through knight-errantry.
units.literal: The people of the Zhou region relied on trade for their livelihood, but Ju Meng made his name among the feudal lords through knight-errantry.

units.zh: 吳楚反時，條侯為太尉，乘傳車將至河南，得劇孟，喜曰：「吳楚舉大事而不求孟，吾知其無能為已矣。」
units.en: When the kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in rebellion, the Marquis of Tiao was serving as Grand Commandant. On his way to Henan by relay carriage, he secured the allegiance of Ju Meng and exclaimed with delight: "Wu and Chu have launched their great revolt without enlisting Meng — I know they cannot accomplish anything for themselves."
units.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, the Marquis of Tiao served as Grand Commandant, and riding a relay cart on his way to Henan, he secured Ju Meng, and said with delight: "Wu and Chu have launched a great enterprise yet did not seek out Meng — I know they cannot accomplish anything for themselves."

units.zh: 天下騷動，宰相得之若得一敵國云。
units.en: When the empire was in turmoil, winning Ju Meng to one's side was said to be worth as much as conquering an enemy state.
units.literal: When the empire was in turmoil, for the chancellor to secure him was like gaining an entire rival state.

units.zh: 劇孟行大類朱家，而好博，多少年之戲。
units.en: In conduct, Ju Meng closely resembled Zhu Jia, though he had a fondness for gambling and the diversions of young men.
units.literal: Ju Meng's conduct was largely similar to that of Zhu Jia, though he was fond of gambling and had many youthful pastimes.

units.zh: 然劇孟母死，自遠方送喪蓋千乘。
units.en: When Ju Meng's mother died, mourners came from distant places to attend the funeral — the carriages numbered close to a thousand.
units.literal: When Ju Meng's mother died, those who came from distant places to attend the funeral filled about a thousand carriages.

units.zh: 及劇孟死，家無餘十金之財。
units.en: When Ju Meng himself died, his household had not so much as ten pieces of gold to its name.
units.literal: When Ju Meng himself died, his household had not even ten pieces of gold remaining.

units.zh: 而符離人王孟亦以俠稱江淮之閒。
units.en: Wang Meng of Fuli was likewise celebrated as a knight-errant throughout the region between the Yangtze and the Huai.
units.literal: Wang Meng of Fuli was also celebrated for his chivalry in the region between the Yangtze and the Huai rivers.

units.zh: 是時濟南瞷氏、陳周庸亦以豪聞，景帝聞之，使使盡誅此屬。
units.en: Around this time, the Jian clan of Jinan and Zhou Yong of Chen were also renowned as local strongmen. Emperor Jing heard of them and dispatched agents to have them all put to death.
units.literal: At this time, the Jian clan of Jinan and Zhou Yong of Chen were also known as local strongmen; Emperor Jing heard of them and dispatched envoys to have them all executed.

units.zh: 其後代諸白、梁韓無辟、陽翟薛兄、陜韓孺紛紛復出焉。
units.en: After them, new figures emerged one after another: the Bai clan of Dai, Han Wubi of Liang, Xue Xiong of Yangzhai, and Han Ru of Shan.
units.literal: Afterwards, the Bai of Dai, Han Wubi of Liang, Xue Xiong of Yangzhai, and Han Ru of Shan emerged one after another.

units.zh: 郭解，軹人也，字翁伯，善相人者許負外孫也。
units.en: Guo Jie was a native of Zhi, with the courtesy name Wengbo. He was the maternal grandson of the famous physiognomist Xu Fu.
units.literal: Guo Jie was from Zhi, with the courtesy name Wengbo; he was the grandson on his mother's side of the famous physiognomist Xu Fu.

units.zh: 解父以任俠，孝文時誅死。
units.en: His father had practiced knight-errantry and was executed for it during the reign of Emperor Wen.
units.literal: Jie's father was executed during the reign of Emperor Wen on account of his knight-errant activities.

units.zh: 解為人短小精悍，不飲酒。
units.en: Guo Jie was short and slight in build, but tough and sharp, and he did not drink.
units.literal: Jie was short and slight in stature, but tough and capable, and did not drink wine.

units.zh: 少時陰賊，慨不快意，身所殺甚眾。
units.en: In his youth he was secretive and ruthless; whenever something displeased him, the men he personally killed were very many.
units.literal: In his youth he was secretive and ruthless; whenever he felt indignant, those he personally killed were very many.

units.zh: 以軀借交報仇，藏命作姦剽攻，（不）休（及）［乃］鑄錢掘冢，固不可勝數。
units.en: He risked his life to avenge his friends, harbored fugitives, committed robberies and raids, counterfeited coins, and plundered tombs — his crimes were beyond counting.
units.literal: He risked his body for friends to take revenge, harbored fugitives, committed robberies and assaults, and also counterfeited coins and robbed tombs — such things were beyond counting.

units.zh: 適有天幸，窘急常得脫，若遇赦。
units.en: Yet as if blessed by heaven, whenever he was cornered he always managed to slip free, or happened to fall under an amnesty.
units.literal: Yet by fortunate coincidence, whenever he was in dire straits he always managed to escape, as if meeting with an amnesty.

units.zh: 及解年長，更折節為儉，以德報怨，厚施而薄望。
units.en: As Guo Jie grew older, he reformed himself and became frugal. He repaid grudges with kindness, gave generously, and expected little in return.
units.literal: When Jie grew older, he changed his ways and became frugal, repaid resentment with virtue, gave generously and expected little in return.

units.zh: 然其自喜為俠益甚。
units.en: Yet his relish for the role of knight-errant only deepened with time.
units.literal: Yet his delight in acting as a knight-errant only grew stronger.

units.zh: 既已振人之命，不矜其功，其陰賊著於心，卒發於睚金故云。
units.en: Though he saved men's lives without taking any credit, the old ruthless instinct was etched deep in his heart and would still flare up at the slightest provocation.
units.literal: Though he had saved people's lives and did not boast of his deeds, the secretive ruthlessness ingrained in his heart would still erupt over the slightest offense.

units.zh: 而少年慕其行，亦輒為報仇，不使知也。
units.en: The young men who admired him would avenge perceived slights on his behalf, without even letting him know.
units.literal: The young men who admired his conduct would also take revenge on his behalf without letting him know.

units.zh: 解姊子負解之勢，與人飲，使之嚼。
units.en: Guo Jie's nephew, trading on his uncle's power, was once drinking with a man and tried to force him to drain his cup.
units.literal: Guo Jie's sister's son, relying on Guo Jie's power, was drinking with someone and forced the person to drain his cup.

units.zh: 非其任，彊必灌之。
units.en: When the man could not handle more wine, the nephew insisted on forcing it down his throat.
units.literal: When the man could not manage it, the nephew insisted on pouring more wine down his throat.

units.zh: 人怒，拔刀刺殺解姊子，亡去。
units.en: The man flew into a rage, drew his sword, and stabbed the nephew to death, then fled.
units.literal: The man became enraged, drew his sword, stabbed and killed Guo Jie's nephew, and fled.

units.zh: 解姊怒曰：「以翁伯之義，人殺吾子，賊不得。」
units.en: Guo Jie's sister was furious and cried: "With all of Wengbo's vaunted sense of justice, someone has killed my son, yet the murderer has not been caught!"
units.literal: Guo Jie's sister said in anger: "With all of Wengbo's sense of honor, someone has killed my son, yet the murderer has not been caught."

units.zh: 棄其尸於道，弗葬，欲以辱解。
units.en: She left her son's corpse lying in the road and refused to bury him, hoping to shame Guo Jie into action.
units.literal: She abandoned her son's corpse on the road and refused to bury it, intending to shame Guo Jie.

units.zh: 解使人微知賊處。
units.en: Guo Jie sent agents to quietly discover the killer's whereabouts.
units.literal: Guo Jie sent someone to secretly learn the killer's whereabouts.

units.zh: 賊窘自歸，具以實告解。
units.en: The killer, finding himself cornered, came and surrendered to Guo Jie of his own accord, telling him the whole truth.
units.literal: The killer, finding himself cornered, came to surrender on his own, and told Guo Jie the whole truth.

units.zh: 解曰：「公殺之固當，吾兒不直。」
units.en: Guo Jie said: "You were right to kill him. My nephew was in the wrong."
units.literal: Guo Jie said: "You were right to kill him — my nephew was in the wrong."

units.zh: 遂去其賊，罪其姊子，乃收而葬之。
units.en: He let the killer go, laid the blame on his own nephew, and then collected the body and gave it a proper burial.
units.literal: He thereupon released the killer, placed the blame on his nephew, and then gathered the body and buried it.

units.zh: 諸公聞之，皆多解之義，益附焉。
units.en: When people heard this story, they all praised Guo Jie's sense of justice, and even more men rallied to his side.
units.literal: When people heard of this, they all praised Guo Jie's sense of justice and rallied to him even more.

units.zh: 解出入，人皆避之。
units.en: Whenever Guo Jie passed through the streets, everyone made way for him.
units.literal: When Guo Jie came and went, people all made way for him.

units.zh: 有一人獨箕倨視之，解遣人問其名姓。
units.en: One man alone sat sprawled with his legs outstretched and stared at him. Guo Jie sent someone to ask the man's name.
units.literal: There was one man who alone sat with legs spread apart and stared at him; Guo Jie sent someone to ask his name.

units.zh: 客欲殺之。
units.en: His followers wanted to kill the man on the spot.
units.literal: His followers wanted to kill the man.

units.zh: 解曰：「居邑屋至不見敬，是吾德不修也，彼何罪！」
units.en: Guo Jie said: "When I live in my own town and go about yet am shown no respect, it is because my own virtue is lacking. What crime has the man committed?"
units.literal: Guo Jie said: "When I live in my own town and go about yet am shown no respect, it is because my virtue is lacking. What crime is it of his!"

units.zh: 乃陰屬尉史曰：「是人，吾所急也，至踐更時脫之。」
units.en: He then secretly instructed the local constable: "This man is under my protection. When his turn comes for conscript labor, exempt him."
units.literal: He then secretly instructed the local constable: "This man is someone I care about — when his turn comes for conscript labor, exempt him."

units.zh: 每至踐更，數過，吏弗求。
units.en: Each time the conscript labor rotation came around, his turn was passed over again and again, and the officials never called on him.
units.literal: Each time the conscript labor rotation came, it passed him by several times, and the officials did not call upon him.

units.zh: 怪之，問其故，乃解使脫之。
units.en: The man found this puzzling and asked why, only to discover that Guo Jie had arranged his exemption.
units.literal: The man found this strange and asked the reason, only to discover that Guo Jie had arranged his exemption.

units.zh: 箕踞者乃肉袒謝罪。
units.en: The man who had sat sprawling came to Guo Jie, bared his shoulders, and begged forgiveness.
units.literal: The man who had sat sprawling then bared his shoulders and apologized for his offense.

units.zh: 少年聞之，愈益慕解之行。
units.en: When the young men heard this story, their admiration for Guo Jie's conduct only grew.
units.literal: When the young men heard of this, they admired Guo Jie's conduct even more.

units.zh: 雒陽人有相仇者，邑中賢豪居閒者以十數，終不聽。
units.en: There were people in Luoyang locked in a bitter feud. More than ten of the town's leading men had tried to mediate, but neither side would listen.
units.literal: There were people in Luoyang locked in a feud; more than ten of the town's worthies and strongmen tried to mediate, but the parties would not listen.

units.zh: 客乃見郭解。
units.en: At last someone went to Guo Jie for help.
units.literal: A guest then went to see Guo Jie.

units.zh: 解夜見仇家，仇家曲聽解。
units.en: Guo Jie visited the feuding party by night, and the man yielded and agreed to accept his mediation.
units.literal: Guo Jie visited the feuding family by night, and the family yielded and agreed to listen to him.

units.zh: 解乃謂仇家曰：「吾聞雒陽諸公在此閒，多不聽者。
units.en: Guo Jie then said to the man: "I hear that many of the Luoyang worthies have tried to settle this dispute, and you have refused them all.
units.literal: Guo Jie then said to the feuding man: "I hear that many of the Luoyang worthies have tried to mediate this matter, and you have refused to listen to most of them.

units.zh: 今子幸而聽解，解柰何乃從他縣奪人邑中賢大夫權乎！」
units.en: Now you are willing to listen to me, but how can I, an outsider from another county, presume to usurp the authority of the worthy men of your own town?"
units.literal: Now you have been willing to listen to me, Guo Jie — but how can I, from another county, take away the authority of the worthy men of your own town!"

units.zh: 乃夜去，不使人知，曰：「且無用，（待我）待我去，令雒陽豪居其閒，乃聽之。」
units.en: He then slipped away in the night without letting anyone know, saying: "Do not settle this yet. Wait until I am gone, then let one of the Luoyang worthies mediate, and accept his terms."
units.literal: He then departed in the night without letting anyone know, saying: "Do not settle this yet. Wait until I have left, then let one of the Luoyang strongmen mediate, and agree to his terms."

units.zh: 解執恭敬，不敢乘車入其縣廷。
units.en: Guo Jie was scrupulously respectful and never presumed to ride in a carriage when visiting the county offices.
units.literal: Guo Jie was scrupulously respectful, and never dared ride in a carriage when entering the county offices.

units.zh: 之旁郡國，為人請求事，事可出，出之；
units.en: When he traveled to neighboring commanderies and kingdoms to intercede on someone's behalf, he would see the matter through if it could be resolved.
units.literal: When he went to neighboring commanderies and kingdoms to intercede on someone's behalf, if the matter could be accomplished, he accomplished it;

units.zh: 不可者，各厭其意，然後乃敢嘗酒食。
units.en: If the matter could not be resolved, he made sure each party felt they had been heard, and only then would he allow himself to accept food or drink.
units.literal: If the matter could not be accomplished, he would ensure each party was satisfied, and only then would he dare to taste wine or food.

units.zh: 諸公以故嚴重之，爭為用。
units.en: For this reason, the local worthies held him in deep respect and vied with one another to be of service.
units.literal: For this reason, the local worthies regarded him with great respect and gravity, and competed to be of service to him.

units.zh: 邑中少年及旁近縣賢豪，夜半過門常十餘車，請得解客舍養之。
units.en: The young men of the town and the leading men of neighboring counties would arrive at his door at midnight, often with more than ten carriages, begging for the privilege of hosting his guests and providing for them.
units.literal: The young men of the town and the worthies and strongmen of neighboring counties would pass his door at midnight with often more than ten carriages, requesting to lodge Guo Jie's guests and provide for them.

units.zh: 及徙豪富茂陵也，解家貧，不中訾，吏恐，不敢不徙。
units.en: When the government ordered the relocation of wealthy and powerful families to Maoling, Guo Jie's family was too poor to meet the property threshold, but the officials were afraid of him and did not dare leave him behind.
units.literal: When the wealthy and powerful were relocated to Maoling, Guo Jie's family was poor and did not meet the property qualification, yet the officials were afraid and did not dare to leave him behind.

units.zh: 衛將軍為言：「郭解家貧不中徙。」
units.en: General Wei Qing spoke to the emperor on his behalf, saying: "The Guo Jie household is poor and does not qualify for relocation."
units.literal: General Wei Qing spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Guo Jie household is poor and does not qualify for relocation."

units.zh: 上曰：「布衣權至使將軍為言，此其家不貧。」
units.en: The emperor said: "A commoner whose influence is great enough to make a general speak on his behalf — his household is not poor."
units.literal: The emperor said: "A commoner whose influence extends to making a general speak on his behalf — his household cannot be poor."

units.zh: 解家遂徙。
units.en: And so the Guo Jie household was relocated after all.
units.literal: So the Guo Jie household was relocated after all.

units.zh: 諸公送者出千餘萬。
units.en: The farewell gifts from the worthies who saw him off totaled more than ten million cash.
units.literal: The farewell gifts contributed by the various worthies who saw him off amounted to more than ten million cash.

units.zh: 軹人楊季主子為縣掾，舉徙解。
units.en: It was the son of Yang Jizhu, a fellow native of Zhi who served as a county clerk, who had nominated Guo Jie for the relocation.
units.literal: The son of Yang Jizhu of Zhi served as a county clerk and had nominated Guo Jie for relocation.

units.zh: 解兄子斷楊掾頭。
units.en: Guo Jie's nephew cut off the head of the young clerk Yang.
units.literal: Guo Jie's brother's son cut off the head of Clerk Yang.

units.zh: 由此楊氏與郭氏為仇。
units.en: From this point on, the Yang and Guo clans became bitter enemies.
units.literal: From this the Yang clan and the Guo clan became enemies.

units.zh: 解入關，關中賢豪知與不知，聞其聲，爭交驩解。
units.en: When Guo Jie arrived in the Guanzhong region, the local worthies and strongmen — whether they knew him personally or not — had all heard his name and competed to befriend him.
units.literal: When Guo Jie entered the Pass, the worthies and strongmen of the Guanzhong region, whether they knew him or not, having heard his reputation, competed to befriend him.

units.zh: 解為人短小，不飲酒，出未嘗有騎。
units.en: Guo Jie was short in stature and did not drink. When he went out, he never rode with a mounted escort.
units.literal: Guo Jie was short and small in stature, did not drink wine, and when he went out he never had a mounted escort.

units.zh: 已又殺楊季主。
units.en: Before long, someone also killed Yang Jizhu himself.
units.literal: Then someone killed Yang Jizhu as well.

units.zh: 楊季主家上書，人又殺之闕下。
units.en: The Yang family submitted a memorial to the throne, but the person who delivered it was murdered right at the palace gates.
units.literal: The Yang Jizhu family submitted a memorial to the throne, but the person who delivered it was killed at the gates of the palace.

units.zh: 上聞，乃下吏捕解。
units.en: When the emperor heard of this, he ordered the authorities to arrest Guo Jie.
units.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he ordered officials to arrest Guo Jie.

units.zh: 解亡，置其母家室夏陽，身至臨晉。
units.en: Guo Jie fled, settling his mother and household at Xiayang while he himself made for Linjin.
units.literal: Guo Jie fled, placing his mother and household at Xiayang, while he himself went to Linjin.

units.zh: 臨晉籍少公素不知解，解冒，因求出關。
units.en: Ji Shaogong of Linjin had never met Guo Jie. Guo Jie approached him under a false name and through him arranged to slip past the border checkpoint.
units.literal: Ji Shaogong of Linjin did not previously know Guo Jie; Guo Jie came to him under an assumed identity and through him sought to pass through the barrier.

units.zh: 籍少公已出解，解轉入太原，所過輒告主人家。
units.en: After Ji Shaogong had helped him through the checkpoint, Guo Jie traveled on into Taiyuan, revealing his identity to his hosts at each stop along the way.
units.literal: After Ji Shaogong had helped Guo Jie pass through, Guo Jie made his way into Taiyuan, and at each stop he would reveal his identity to his host household.

units.zh: 吏逐之，跡至籍少公。
units.en: The authorities pursued him and traced his trail back to Ji Shaogong.
units.literal: The officials pursued him and traced his trail to Ji Shaogong.

units.zh: 少公自殺，口絕。
units.en: Ji Shaogong killed himself, sealing the secret with his death.
units.literal: Shaogong killed himself, and his mouth was silenced forever.

units.zh: 久之，乃得解。
units.en: After a long search, Guo Jie was finally captured.
units.literal: After a long time, Guo Jie was finally captured.

units.zh: 窮治所犯，為解所殺，皆在赦前。
units.en: When the authorities exhaustively investigated his crimes, they found that all the killings attributed to Guo Jie had occurred before the most recent amnesty.
units.literal: When all his offenses were exhaustively investigated, the killings attributed to Guo Jie had all occurred before the amnesty.

units.zh: 軹有儒生侍使者坐，客譽郭解，生曰：「郭解專以姦犯公法，何謂賢！」
units.en: In Zhi, a Confucian scholar was seated in the company of the imperial envoy. When a guest began praising Guo Jie, the scholar spoke up: "Guo Jie does nothing but use wickedness to break the law — what is worthy about that!"
units.literal: In Zhi, there was a Confucian scholar sitting in attendance on the imperial envoy; a guest was praising Guo Jie, and the scholar said: "Guo Jie does nothing but use wickedness to violate the public law — what is worthy about that!"

units.zh: 解客聞，殺此生，斷其舌。
units.en: When Guo Jie's followers heard what the scholar had said, they killed him and cut out his tongue.
units.literal: When Guo Jie's followers heard of this, they killed the scholar and cut out his tongue.

units.zh: 吏以此責解，解實不知殺者。
units.en: The authorities charged Guo Jie with the crime, but in truth he did not know who had done the killing.
units.literal: The officials blamed Guo Jie for this, but in truth Guo Jie did not know who the killer was.

units.zh: 殺者亦竟絕，莫知為誰。
units.en: The killer vanished completely, and no one ever discovered who it was.
units.literal: The killer also vanished without a trace, and no one ever learned who it was.

units.zh: 吏奏解無罪。
units.en: The officials submitted their finding that Guo Jie was not guilty.
units.literal: The officials reported that Guo Jie was not guilty.

units.zh: 御史大夫公孫弘議曰：「解布衣為任俠行權，以睚眥殺人，解雖弗知，此罪甚於解殺之。
units.en: The Imperial Counselor Gongsun Hong argued: "Guo Jie is a commoner who practices knight-errantry and wields unauthorized power. Men are killed over the slightest grudge on his account. Even if he did not know of it, this crime is greater than if he had killed them with his own hand.
units.literal: The Imperial Counselor Gongsun Hong argued: "Guo Jie, a commoner, practices knight-errantry and exercises unauthorized power; men are killed over the merest grudge on his account. Even though Guo Jie may not have known, this crime is worse than if Guo Jie had killed them himself.

units.zh: 當大逆無道。」
units.en: He should be condemned for the crime of high treason."
units.literal: He should be charged with the crime of great treason and depravity."

units.zh: 遂族郭解翁伯。
units.en: And so the entire clan of Guo Jie was exterminated.
units.literal: And so the entire clan of Guo Jie, styled Wengbo, was exterminated.

units.zh: 自是之後，為俠者極眾，敖而無足數者。
units.en: From this time onward, those who styled themselves knights-errant were extremely numerous, but they were arrogant and of no account.
units.literal: From this time onward, those who practiced knight-errantry were extremely numerous, but they were arrogant and not worth counting.

units.zh: 然關中長安樊仲子，槐裏趙王孫，長陵高公子，西河郭公仲，太原鹵公孺，臨淮兒長卿，東陽田君孺，雖為俠而逡逡有退讓君子之風。
units.en: Among them, Fan Zhongzi of Chang'an in the Guanzhong region, Zhao Wangsun of Huaili, Gao Gongzi of Changling, Guo Gongzhong of Xihe, Lu Gongru of Taiyuan, Er Changqing of Linhuai, and Tian Junru of Dongyang — though all knights-errant — carried themselves with the modesty and restraint of true gentlemen.
units.literal: However, Fan Zhongzi of Chang'an in Guanzhong, Zhao Wangsun of Huaili, Gao Gongzi of Changling, Guo Gongzhong of Xihe, Lu Gongru of Taiyuan, Er Changqing of Linhuai, and Tian Junru of Dongyang, though they were knights-errant, were modest and had the restrained bearing of gentlemen.

units.zh: 至若北道姚氏，西道諸杜，南道仇景，東道趙他、羽公子，南陽趙調之徒，此盜跖居民閒者耳，曷足道哉！
units.en: As for the Yao clan of the northern road, the Du family of the western road, Qiu Jing of the southern road, Zhao Ta and Lord Yu of the eastern road, and Zhao Diao of Nanyang and their kind — they were nothing more than Robber Zhis lurking among the common folk, and hardly worth discussing!
units.literal: As for the Yao clan of the northern road, the various Du of the western road, Qiu Jing of the southern road, Zhao Ta and Lord Yu of the eastern road, and the like of Zhao Diao of Nanyang — these were merely Robber Zhis living among the people, and hardly worth mentioning!

units.zh: 此乃鄉者朱家之羞也。
units.en: They would have been a disgrace in the eyes of the great Zhu Jia.
units.literal: They would be a source of shame to the earlier Zhu Jia.

units.zh: 太史公曰：吾視郭解，狀貌不及中人，言語不足採者。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: I have looked upon Guo Jie myself. In appearance, he was less than ordinary, and in speech there was nothing remarkable about him.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: I have observed Guo Jie — his appearance was less impressive than an average person, and his speech was not worth noting.

units.zh: 然天下無賢與不肖，知與不知，皆慕其聲，言俠者皆引以為名。
units.en: Yet throughout the empire, whether worthy or base, whether they had met him or not, all people admired his name, and whenever anyone spoke of knight-errantry, they invoked Guo Jie as the standard.
units.literal: Yet throughout the world, whether worthy or unworthy, whether they knew him or not, all admired his reputation, and whenever people spoke of knight-errantry they cited him as the paragon.

units.zh: 諺曰：「人貌榮名，豈有既乎！」
units.en: As the proverb says: "When a man's looks and his glorious fame are so far apart, will the world's wonder ever cease?"
units.literal: The proverb says: "A man's looks and his glorious fame — can there ever be an end to it?"

units.zh: 於戲，惜哉！
units.en: Alas, how tragic!
units.literal: Alas, what a pity!

units.zh: 樞肆志尋覽，殆將周遍，乃喟然歎曰：「吾聞貴爵位者以巢、由為桎梏，愛山林者以伊、呂為管庫，束名實則芻芥柱下之言，翫清虛則糠秕席上之說，稽之篤論，亦各從其好也。
units.en: Shu read through them almost entirely and sighed: "I hear that men who prize office take Chao Fu and Xu You as shackles, and men who love the hills take Yi and Lü as storekeepers; those who bind name to fact treat Laozi as straw, and those who play at emptiness treat banquet talk as chaff. In earnest judgment each follows his own bent.
units.literal: Shu with full intent searched and read them, nearly covering all; he then sighed and said: "I have heard that those who prize rank and title take Chao Fu and Xu You as fetters, and those who love mountains and forests take Yi and Lü as granary keepers; binding name and reality makes Laozi's words mere hay; playing with emptiness and purity makes seat-side doctrines mere chaff; checked against earnest discourse, each also follows his own preference.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。
units.en: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
units.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

units.zh: 韓非之智，不免秦獄，劉歆之學，猶弊亡新，音塵不嗣，每以耿灼。
units.en: Han Fei's wisdom did not escape Qin's prison; Liu Xin's learning still perished in Xin. Voice and dust do not continue—I burn with grief.
units.literal: Han Fei's wisdom did not escape Qin's prison; Liu Xin's learning still perished in Xin; voice and dust do not continue—I am often burning with grief.

units.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武，[9]或以假諸功臣，或以加於戚屬，是以魏曹植表駙馬、奉車趣為一號。
units.en: The consort commandant was created by Han Wudi; [9] it was sometimes given to meritorious ministers and sometimes to kin—hence Cao Zhi in Wei asked to merge consort commandant and carriage attendant into one title.
units.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han; [9] sometimes it was lent to meritorious ministers, sometimes added for kin—hence in Wei, Cao Zhi petitioned to make the consort commandant and the carriage attendant a single title.

units.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武 「由」字原本漫漶，今據各本補。
units.en: On "consort commandant established by Han Wudi": the character you was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.
units.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han—the character "by" in the original was effaced; it is now supplied from the various editions.

units.zh: 高祖，沛豐邑中陽里人也，姓劉氏。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was born in Zhongyang Village in the town of Fengyi, Pei County. His surname was Liu.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was a person of Zhongyang Village, Fengyi Town, Pei County, and his surname was Liu.

units.zh: 蕭何曰：「劉季固多大言，少成事。」
units.en: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji certainly talks big but accomplishes little."
units.literal: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji indeed makes many big claims, accomplishes few matters."

units.zh: 秦二年十月，沛公攻胡陵、方與，還守豐。
units.en: In the tenth month of the second year of Qin, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, then returned to defend Feng.
units.literal: Qin second year tenth month, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, returned to defend Feng.

units.zh: 呂公曰：「臣少好相人，相人多矣，無如季相，願季自愛。
units.en: Lü Gong said: "Since I was young, I've enjoyed reading faces. I've read many people's faces, but none compare to Ji's. I hope Ji takes good care of himself.
units.literal: Lü Gong said: "I from youth favored physiognomy, have read many people's faces, none like Ji's appearance, wish Ji to take care of himself.

units.zh: 臣有息女，願為箕帚妾。」
units.en: I have a young daughter and wish to make her Ji's humble servant."
units.literal: I have a young daughter, wish to make her Ji's broom and dustpan servant."

units.zh: 沛令善公，求之不與，何自妄許與劉季？」
units.en: The magistrate of Pei was your friend and asked for her, but you wouldn't give her. Why are you now rashly promising her to Liu Ji?"
units.literal: The Pei magistrate was friendly with you, requested her and you did not give, why now rashly promise her to Liu Ji?"

units.zh: 呂后曰：「季所居上常有雲氣，故從往常得季。」
units.en: Empress Lü said: "There are always clouds above where you stay. That's why we can always find you by following them."
units.literal: Empress Lu said: 'Where Ji resides above constantly has cloud aura, therefore following it constantly finds Ji.'

units.zh: 諸父老皆曰：「平生所聞劉季奇怪，當貴，且卜筮之，莫如劉季最吉。」
units.en: All the elders said: "In our lifetimes we have heard that Liu Ji is strange and marked for nobility. Moreover, when we divined on it, none was more auspicious than Liu Ji."
units.literal: All the elders said: 'In our lives we have heard Liu Ji is strange and extraordinary, should be noble, moreover divining it, none is more auspicious than Liu Ji.'

units.zh: 已而有娠，遂產高祖。
units.en: Soon after, she became pregnant and gave birth to Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Soon after she became pregnant, and then gave birth to the Supreme Ancestor.

units.zh: 高祖為人，隆準而龍顏，美須髯，左股有七十二黑子。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu had a prominent nose, a face like a dragon, beautiful whiskers and beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor as a person had a high nose and dragon face, beautiful beard and whiskers, and on his left thigh there were seventy-two black moles.

units.zh: 高祖每酤留飲，酒讎數倍。
units.en: Whenever Emperor Gaozu bought wine, he stayed to drink, and the bill was several times higher.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor each time he bought wine would stay and drink, the wine price several times.

units.zh: 高祖常繇咸陽，縱觀秦皇帝，喟然大息，曰：「嗟乎，大丈夫當如此矣！」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu often passed through Xianyang and gazed upon the Qin emperor. He would sigh deeply and say: "Ah, this is how a true man should live!"
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor often performed corvée service at Xianyang and was allowed to observe the Qin emperor; he sighed deeply and said: "Alas, a great man should be like this!"

units.zh: 高祖為亭長，素易諸吏，乃紿為謁曰「賀錢萬」，實不持一錢。
units.en: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu had always treated the officials lightly. He deceived them by having the announcement read "Congratulatory gift: ten thousand cash," though in fact he did not bring a single coin.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was pavilion chief, usually casual with the officials, then deceived to make the announcement saying "Congratulatory money ten thousand," in reality he did not bring a single cash.

units.zh: 呂公者，好相人，見高祖狀貌，因重敬之，引入坐上坐。
units.en: Lü Gong was skilled in reading faces. When he saw Emperor Gaozu's appearance, he was greatly impressed and led him inside to be seated in the place of honor.
units.literal: Lü Gong was good at physiognomy, saw the Supreme Ancestor's appearance, because of this greatly respected him, led him in to sit in the seat of honor.

units.zh: 高祖因狎侮諸客，遂坐上坐，無所詘。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu took advantage of this to treat all the guests with casual familiarity and even insult them. He sat in the place of honor without showing any humility.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor because of this treated the various guests with familiarity and insult, then sat in the seat of honor, was not humble in any way.

units.zh: 酒闌，呂公因目固留高祖。
units.en: As the banquet ended, Lü Gong signaled insistently to keep Emperor Gaozu there.
units.literal: The wine came to an end, Lü Gong because of this gave meaningful looks and firmly kept the Supreme Ancestor.

units.zh: 卒與高祖。
units.en: In the end, she married Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: In the end he married with the Supreme Ancestor.

units.zh: 高祖嘗告歸之田。
units.en: Once, Emperor Gaozu requested leave to return to his fields.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor once requested leave to return to the fields.

units.zh: 老父已去，高祖適從旁舍來，呂后具言客有過，相我子母皆大貴。
units.en: The old man had already left. Emperor Gaozu had just returned from a neighboring house. Empress Lü told him everything: a guest had passed by and read the faces of her, the children, and her mother—they were all greatly noble.
units.literal: The old man had already left; Gaozu had just come from the neighboring house. Empress Lü told him in full that a guest had passed by and read the faces of her and her children—all were greatly noble.

units.zh: 高祖問，曰：「未遠。」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu asked where the old man had gone. She said, "Not far."
units.literal: Gaozu asked, said: 'Not far.'

units.zh: 高祖乃謝曰：「誠如父言，不敢忘德。」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu then thanked him and said: "If what you say is true, I won't forget your kindness."
units.literal: Gaozu then thanked saying: 'Truly as father says, do not dare forget the kindness.'

units.zh: 及高祖貴，遂不知老父處。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu rose to power, he could no longer find the old man.
units.literal: When Gaozu became noble, then did not know the old father's whereabouts.

units.zh: 高祖為亭長，乃鲈竹皮為冠，令求盜之薛治，時時冠之，及貴常冠，所謂「劉氏冠」也。
units.en: While he was pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu made a cap of bamboo sheathing. When he was sent to pursue bandits in the Xue district he wore it from time to time, and after he rose high he still wore it constantly. This is what was called the "Liu family cap."
units.literal: While Gaozu was pavilion chief, he made a cap of bamboo sheathing; he was ordered to pursue bandits in the Xue district and wore it from time to time; after he rose high he still wore it constantly—this is what is called the "Liu family cap."

units.zh: 高祖以亭長為縣送徒驪山，徒多道亡。
units.en: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu was assigned by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li. Many of the convicts fled along the road.
units.literal: Gaozu as pavilion chief was ordered by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li, the convicts many fled on the road.

units.zh: 高祖被酒，夜徑澤中，令一人行前。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and at night went directly through the marsh, ordering one man to go ahead.
units.literal: Gaozu was drunk, at night went straight through the marshes, ordered one person to go ahead.

units.zh: 高祖醉，曰：「壯士行，何畏！」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and said: "A brave man walks on. What is there to fear!"
units.literal: Gaozu was drunk, said: 'A brave man walks forward, what is there to fear!'

units.zh: 後人至，高祖覺。
units.en: Later people arrived, and Emperor Gaozu woke up.
units.literal: Later people arrived, Gaozu awoke.

units.zh: 告高祖，高祖乃心獨喜，自負。
units.en: They told Emperor Gaozu, who was secretly delighted and grew confident in himself.
units.literal: Told Gaozu, Gaozu then in his heart alone rejoiced, considered himself superior.

units.zh: 高祖隱於芒、碭山澤間，呂后與人俱求，常得之。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang. Empress Lü and others searched for him together and always found him.
units.literal: Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang, Empress Lu and others together sought him, constantly found him.

units.zh: 高祖怪問之。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was surprised and asked how.
units.literal: Gaozu strangely questioned her.

units.zh: 高祖又喜。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was delighted once more.
units.literal: Gaozu again was happy.

units.zh: 乃令樊噲召高祖。
units.en: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.
units.literal: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖之眾已數百人矣。
units.en: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.
units.literal: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.

units.zh: 於是樊噲從高祖來。
units.en: So Fan Kuai came to follow Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Therefore Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and came.

units.zh: 蕭、曹恐，踰城保高祖。
units.en: Xiao and Cao were afraid, so they climbed over the wall to join Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Xiao and Cao feared, climbed over the wall to protect Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖乃書帛射城上，與沛父老曰：「天下同苦秦久矣。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, saying to the elders of Pei: "All under heaven have suffered under Qin for a long time.
units.literal: Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, telling the Pei elders: 'The world together has suffered under Qin for a long time.

units.zh: 父老乃帥子弟共殺沛令，開城門迎高祖，欲以為沛令。
units.en: The elders then led the young men together to kill the magistrate of Pei, opened the city gates to welcome Emperor Gaozu, and wanted to make him magistrate of Pei.
units.literal: The elders then led the young men together to kill the Pei magistrate, opened the city gates to welcome Gaozu, wished to make him Pei magistrate.

units.zh: 高祖曰：「天下方擾，諸侯並起，令置將不善，一敗塗地。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu said: "The world is in chaos right now, with feudal lords rising up everywhere. If you appoint a commander who is not capable, one defeat will ruin everything.
units.literal: Gaozu said: 'The world is currently in chaos, feudal lords all rise, if the magistrate appoints generals poorly, one defeat and all lost.

units.zh: 蕭、曹等皆文吏，自愛，恐事不就，後秦種族其家，盡讓高祖。
units.en: Xiao, Cao, and the others were all civil officials who cherished themselves. They feared that if things didn't succeed, Qin would exterminate their families, so they all yielded to Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Xiao, Cao and others all were civil officials, cherished themselves, feared the matter would not succeed, afterward Qin would exterminate their families, all yielded to Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖數讓。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu declined repeatedly.
units.literal: Gaozu repeatedly declined.

units.zh: 眾莫肯為，高祖乃立為沛公。
units.en: No one else was willing to take it, so Emperor Gaozu was established as Lord of Pei.
units.literal: The crowd none would do it, Gaozu then was established as Pei Gong.

units.zh: 十一月，沛公引兵之薛。
units.en: In the eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xue.
units.literal: Eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xi.

units.zh: 秦泗川守壯兵敗於薛，走至戚，沛公左司馬得殺之。
units.en: The Qin governor of Si River Zhuang was defeated at Xue and fled to Qi, where Pei Gong's left commander Sima De killed him.
units.literal: Qin Sishui defender Zhuang's troops defeated at Xue, fled to Qi, Pei Gong's left marshal captured and killed him.

units.zh: 沛公還軍亢父，至方與。
units.en: Pei Gong returned his army to Kangfu and arrived at Fang Yu.
units.literal: Pei Gong returned his army to Kang Fu, arrived at Fang Yu.

units.zh: 雍齒雅不欲屬沛公，及魏招之，即反為魏守豐。
units.en: Yong Chi had long not wanted to serve Pei Gong, and when Wei summoned him, he immediately rebelled and defended Feng for Wei.
units.literal: Yong Chi usually did not wish to belong to Pei Gong, when Wei summoned him, immediately rebelled to guard Feng for Wei.

units.zh: 沛公攻豐，不能取。
units.en: Pei Gong attacked Feng but could not capture it.
units.literal: Pei Gong attacked Feng, could not capture it.

units.zh: 沛公還之沛，怨雍齒與豐子弟畔之。
units.en: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resentful that Yong Chi and the young men of Feng had rebelled against him.
units.literal: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resented Yong Chi and the Feng youths rebelling against him.

units.zh: 沛公往從之，道得張良，遂與俱見景駒，請兵以攻豐。
units.en: Pei Gong went to join him, met Zhang Liang along the way, and together they went to see Jing Ju, requesting troops to attack Feng.
units.literal: Pei Gong went to follow them, on the road obtained Zhang Liang, then together went to see Jing Ju, requested troops to attack Feng.

units.zh: 東陽甯君、沛公引兵西，與戰蕭西，不利，還收兵聚留。
units.en: The Lord of Dongyang Ning and Pei Gong led troops west and battled west of Xiao, but were unsuccessful, so they retreated and gathered troops at Liu.
units.literal: Dongyang Ning Jun, Pei Gong led troops west, fought battle at Xiao west, unfavorable, returned gathered troops at Liu.

units.zh: 四月，項梁擊殺景駒、秦嘉，止薛，沛公往見之。
units.en: In the fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju and Qin Jia, then stopped at Xue. Pei Gong went to see him.
units.literal: Fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju, Qin Jia, stopped at Xue, Pei Gong went to see him.

units.zh: 項梁益沛公卒五千人，五大夫將十人。
units.en: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops by five thousand men and ten generals of the rank of Grand Master.
units.literal: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops five thousand, Grand Master generals ten people.

units.zh: 沛公還，引兵攻豐，拔之。
units.en: Pei Gong returned and led troops to attack Feng, capturing it.
units.literal: Pei Gong returned, led troops to attack Feng, captured it.

units.zh: 六月，沛公如薛，與項梁共立楚懷王孫心為楚懷王。
units.en: In the sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue and together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as King Huai of Chu.
units.literal: Sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue, together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as Chu King Huai.

units.zh: 沛公攻亢父。
units.en: Pei Gong attacked Kangfu.
units.literal: Pei Gong attacked Kang Fu.

units.zh: 沛公與項梁共救田榮，大破章邯東阿。
units.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Liang together went to rescue Tian Rong and greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'e.
units.literal: Pei Gong together with Xiang Liang rescued Tian Rong, greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'a.

units.zh: 田榮歸，沛公、項羽追北，至城陽，攻屠其城。
units.en: Tian Rong returned. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu pursued the defeated enemy north to Chengyang and attacked, massacring the population of the city.
units.literal: Tian Rong returned, Pei Gong, Xiang Yu pursued north, arrived at Chengyang, attacked and slaughtered its city.

units.zh: 沛公、項羽去攻定陶。
units.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.
units.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.

units.zh: 定陶未下，沛公與項羽西略地至雍丘，與秦軍戰，大敗之，斬三川守李由。
units.en: Dingtao had not yet fallen. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu marched west to seize territory as far as Yongqiu, where they battled Qin troops and greatly defeated them, beheading the governor of Sanchuan, Li You.
units.literal: Dingtao not yet fallen, Pei Gong together with Xiang Yu west conquered territory to Yongqiu, fought with Qin army, greatly defeated them, beheaded Sanchuan defender Li You.

units.zh: 沛公、項羽方攻陳留，聞梁死，士卒恐，乃與將軍呂臣引兵而東，徙懷王自盱台都彭城。
units.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu were attacking Chenliu when they heard of Liang's death. The soldiers were terrified, so they joined with General Lü Chen and led troops east, moving King Huai from Xutai to Pengcheng as the capital.
units.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu just attacking Chenliu, heard Liang died, soldiers afraid, then together with general Lu Chen led troops east, moved King Huai from Xutai capital to Pengcheng.

units.zh: 呂臣軍彭城東，項羽軍彭城西，沛公軍碭。
units.en: Lü Chen's army was stationed east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, and Pei Gong's army at Dang.
units.literal: Lu Chen's army east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, Pei Gong's army at Dang.

units.zh: 以沛公為碭郡長，封武安侯，將碭郡兵。
units.en: He appointed Pei Gong as governor of Dang commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuan, and put him in command of Dang commandery troops.
units.literal: Made Pei Gong Dang commandery chief, sealed as Marquis of Wuan, led Dang commandery troops.

units.zh: 獨羽怨秦破項梁，奮勢，願與沛公西入關。
units.en: Only Xiang Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang and was eager to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.
units.literal: Only Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang, exerted his influence, wished to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.

units.zh: 項羽不可遣，獨沛公素寬大長者。」
units.en: Xiang Yu should not be sent. Only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and an elder."
units.literal: Xiang Yu cannot be sent, only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and elder.'

units.zh: 卒不許羽，而遣沛公西收陳王、項梁散卒。
units.en: In the end they did not permit Xiang Yu, but sent Pei Gong west to gather the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang.
units.literal: In the end did not permit Yu, instead sent Pei Gong west to gather King Chen, Xiang Liang's scattered troops.

units.zh: 沛公攻破東郡尉於成武。
units.en: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dong commandery commandant at Chengwu.
units.literal: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dongjun prefect at Chengwu.

units.zh: 十二月，沛公引兵至栗，遇剛武侯，奪其軍四千餘人，并之，與魏將皇欣、武滿軍合，攻秦軍，破之。
units.en: In the twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li and encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized over four thousand of his men, and combined them. He joined with Wei generals Huang Xin and Wu Man's army and attacked Qin troops, defeating them.
units.literal: Twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li, encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized his army more than four thousand people, merged them, combined with Wei generals Huang Xin, Wu Man armies, attacked Qin army, defeated it.

units.zh: 二月，沛公從碭北攻昌邑，遇彭越。
units.en: In the second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi and encountered Peng Yue.
units.literal: Second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi, encountered Peng Yue.

units.zh: 沛公西過高陽，酈食其為里監門，曰：「諸將過此者多，吾視沛公大度。」
units.en: Pei Gong passed west through Gaoyang. Li Yiji was the village gatekeeper and said: "Many generals have passed through here. I can see that Pei Gong has great magnanimity."
units.literal: Pei Gong west passed Gaoyang, Li Yiji was village gatekeeper, said: 'Various generals who passed this place many, I observe Pei Gong has great magnanimity.'

units.zh: 乃求見沛公。
units.en: So he sought to see Pei Gong.
units.literal: Then requested to see Pei Gong.

units.zh: 沛公方踞床，使兩女子洗。
units.en: Pei Gong was sitting cross-legged on a bed, having two women wash his feet.
units.literal: Pei Gong just then squatting on bed, made two women wash.

units.zh: 於是沛公起，攝衣謝之，延上坐。
units.en: So Pei Gong rose, straightened his clothes, and apologized. He invited him to sit in the honored position.
units.literal: Thereupon Pei Gong rose, gathered clothes thanked him, invited to upper seat.

units.zh: 食其說沛公襲陳留。
units.en: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.
units.literal: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.

units.zh: 沛公以為廣野君，以其弟商為將，將陳留兵。
units.en: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.
units.literal: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.

units.zh: 時趙別將司馬卬方欲渡河入關，沛公乃北攻平陰，絕河津。
units.en: At this time, Sima Ang, a separate Zhao general, was about to cross the Yellow River and enter the passes. Pei Gong therefore attacked Pingyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.
units.literal: At this time, the Zhao general Sima Ang was about to cross the river into the passes. Pei Gong attacked Beiyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.

units.zh: 沛公引兵過宛西。
units.en: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.
units.literal: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.

units.zh: 張良諫曰：「沛公雖欲急入關，秦兵尚眾，距險。
units.en: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.
units.literal: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.

units.zh: 沛公至霸上。
units.en: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.
units.literal: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.

units.zh: 諸將或言誅秦王，沛公曰：「始懷王遣我，固以能寬容，且人已服降，殺之不祥。」
units.en: Some of the generals said that the King of Qin should be executed. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient. Moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered; to kill him would be inauspicious."
units.literal: Some of the generals said to execute the King of Qin. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient; moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered, and to kill him would be inauspicious."

units.zh: 三月，漢王自臨晉渡河，魏王豹降，將兵從。
units.en: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.
units.literal: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.

units.zh: 南渡平陰津，至洛陽，新城三老董公遮說漢王曰：「臣聞『順德者昌，逆德者亡』，『兵出無名，事故不成』。
units.en: He crossed south at Pingyin Ford and reached Luoyang. Dong Gong, the elder of Xincheng, stopped the King of Han and advised him: "I have heard, 'Those who follow virtue prosper; those who oppose virtue perish,' and, 'When troops are sent out without a proper name, the enterprise will not succeed.'
units.literal: He crossed south at Pingyin ford and reached Luoyang. The elder of Xincheng, Dong Gong, blocked and advised King Han: "I have heard that 'those who follow virtue prosper, those who oppose virtue perish,' and 'when troops are sent out without just cause, affairs will not succeed.'

units.zh: 羽見紀信，問：「漢王安在？」
units.en: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"
units.literal: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"

units.zh: 漢王從之。
units.en: King Han followed their advice.
units.literal: King Han followed their advice.

units.zh: 吾與諸侯約，先入關者王之，吾當王關中。
units.en: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.
units.literal: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.

units.zh: 民又益喜，唯恐沛公不為秦王。
units.en: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.
units.literal: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.

units.zh: 背約，更立沛公為漢王，王巴、蜀、漢中四十一縣，都南鄭。
units.en: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.
units.literal: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.

units.zh: 漢王怨羽之背約，欲攻之，丞相蕭何諫，乃止。
units.en: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.
units.literal: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.

units.zh: 漢王曰：「善，非夫子無所聞。」
units.en: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."
units.literal: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."

units.zh: 及壯，試吏，為泗上亭長，廷中吏無所不狎侮。
units.en: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official and became pavilion chief of Sishang. Among the officials at court there was none he did not treat with familiar disrespect.
units.literal: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official, became the pavilion chief of Sishang, and among the officials in the court there was none he did not treat with familiarity and insult.

units.zh: 沛公然其計，從之。
units.en: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.
units.literal: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.

units.zh: 五月，漢王引兵從故道出襲雍。
units.en: In the fifth month, King Han led troops from the old road to attack Yong by surprise.
units.literal: In the fifth month, King Han led troops from the old road to attack Yong by surprise.

units.zh: 漢王出滎陽，至成皋。
units.en: King Han left Xingyang and reached Chenggao.
units.literal: King Han left Xingyang and reached Chenggao.

units.zh: 母媼嘗息大澤之陂，夢與神遇。
units.en: Once, while resting by the dike of a vast marsh, his mother dreamed that she encountered a divine being.
units.literal: His mother the old woman once rested by the dike of the great marsh, and dreamed of encountering a god.

units.zh: 是時雷電晦冥，父太公往視，則見交龍於上。
units.en: At that moment, thunder crashed and darkness fell. His father, Taigong, went to investigate and saw two dragons entwined in the sky above.
units.literal: At this time thunder and lightning were dark and obscure, father Taigong went to look, then saw two dragons entwining above.

units.zh: 呂公女即呂后也，生孝惠帝、魯元公主。
units.en: This daughter of Lü Gong would become Empress Lü. She gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.
units.literal: Lü Gong's daughter was namely Empress Lü, gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.

units.zh: 呂后與兩子居田中，有一老父過請飲，呂后因餔之。
units.en: Empress Lü lived in the countryside with their two children. An old man passed by and asked for a drink. Empress Lü fed him.
units.literal: Empress Lü and the two children resided in the fields, there was an old father who passed by requesting drink, Empress Lü because of this fed him.

units.zh: 孝文皇帝，高祖中子也，母曰薄姬。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowen was the middle son of Emperor Gaozu, born to Lady Bo.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was Gaozu's middle son, his mother was named Lady Bo.

units.zh: 贊曰：孝文皇帝即位二十三年，宮室苑囿車騎服御無所增益。
units.en: The commentator states: Emperor Xiaowen reigned for twenty-three years without adding to the palaces, parks, carriages, horses, or furnishings.
units.literal: The commentator says: Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne for twenty-three years, and the palaces, parks, carriages, horses, and furnishings were not increased at all.

units.zh: 高祖十一年，誅陳豨，定代地，立為代王，都中都。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after executing Chen Xi and pacifying the Dai region, he was established as King of Dai with his capital at Zhongdu.
units.literal: In Gaozu's eleventh year, executed Chen Xi, pacified Dai territory, established as King of Dai, capital at Zhongdu.

units.zh: 皇帝即日夕入未央宮。
units.en: The emperor entered Weiyang Palace that same evening.
units.literal: That evening the emperor entered Weiyang Palace.

units.zh: 遂即天子位。
units.en: He immediately ascended the imperial throne.
units.literal: He then immediately ascended the imperial throne.

units.zh: 七年夏六月己亥，帝崩于未央宮。
units.en: On the day Jihai in the sixth month of summer in the seventh year, the emperor passed away in Weiyang Palace.
units.literal: In the seventh year, summer, sixth month, day Jihai, the emperor died in Weiyang Palace.

units.zh: 上曰： 「楚王，季父也，春秋高，閱天下之義理多矣，明於國家之體。
units.en: The emperor replied: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. Advanced in years and experienced in the world's moral principles, he understands the proper order of the state.
units.literal: The emperor said: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. He is advanced in age, has seen much of the world's principles and righteousness, understands the structure of the state.

units.zh: 吳王於朕，兄也；
units.en: The King of Wu is like an elder brother to me;
units.literal: The King of Wu is an elder brother to me;

units.zh: 淮南王，弟也：皆秉德以陪朕，豈為不豫哉！
units.en: The King of Huainan is like a younger brother to me. All of them uphold virtue to support me—how could they not stand ready as successors!
units.literal: The King of Huainan is my younger brother: all uphold virtue to assist me, how could they not be prepared!

units.zh: 子啟最長，敦厚慈仁，請建以為太子。」
units.en: Prince Qi is the eldest son, honest and sincere, kind and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'
units.literal: Prince Qi is the eldest, honest, kind, and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'

units.zh: 皇太后曰：「立太子母竇氏為皇后。」
units.en: The Empress Dowager declared: 'Establish Lady Dou, mother of the crown prince, as empress.'
units.literal: The Empress Dowager said: 'Establish the crown prince's mother Lady Dou as empress.'

units.zh: 因立皇子武為代王，參為太原王，揖為梁王。
units.en: As a result, he established his sons Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.
units.literal: Consequently he established the imperial princes Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.

units.zh: 身衣弋綈，所幸慎夫人衣不曳地，帷帳無文繡，以示敦朴，為天下先。
units.en: He himself wore coarse silk garments, and his favored Lady Shen's robes did not trail on the ground. The curtains and canopies lacked embroidered patterns, demonstrating frugality and setting an example for the world.
units.literal: He himself wore coarse silk, and the favored Lady Shen's robes did not drag on the ground; the curtains and canopies had no embroidered patterns, to demonstrate frugality and lead the world by example.

units.zh: 孝文時，吳太子入見，得侍皇太子飲博。
units.en: In Emperor Wen’s reign the crown prince of Wu attended court and was allowed to drink and play liubo with the imperial heir.
units.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen the Wu heir came to court and was admitted to drink and play liubo with the heir apparent.

units.zh: 博爭道，不恭，皇太子引博局提吳太子，殺之。
units.en: They quarreled over the rules; the Wu heir showed disrespect, and the crown prince seized the heavy board and struck him dead.
units.literal: A dispute over a move in the game turned disrespectful; the imperial heir snatched up the gaming board and dashed it against the Wu prince, killing him.

units.zh: 朝錯為太子家令，得幸皇太子，數從容言吳過可削。
units.en: Chao Cuo was serving as household steward to the crown prince and had won his favor. He repeatedly said in private that Wu's offenses gave grounds for reducing its territory.
units.literal: Chao Cuo served as household steward to the crown prince. Favored by the crown prince, he repeatedly said in private that Wu's offenses could be grounds for reducing its territory.

units.zh: 及景帝即位，錯為御史大夫，說上曰：「昔高帝初定天下，昆弟少，諸子弱，大封同姓，故孽子悼惠王王齊七十二城，庶弟元王王楚四十城，兄子王吳五十餘城。
units.en: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo became Imperial Counselor. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, he had few brothers and his sons were young, so he gave large fiefs to men of his own surname. Thus King Daohui, his son by a concubine, ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; King Yuan, his younger half-brother, ruled Chu with forty cities; and his nephew ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, Cuo became Grandee Secretary. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, his brothers were few and his sons were young, so he made large grants to men of his own surname. Thus King Daohui, his son by a concubine, ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; King Yuan, his younger half-brother, ruled Chu with forty cities; and his elder brother's son ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.

units.zh: 孝景前三年正月甲子，初起兵於廣陵。
units.en: On jiǎzǐ in the first month of Xiaojing’s third year the rebellion opened at Guangling.
units.literal: On the jiǎzǐ day of the first month in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing, he first raised troops at Guangling.

units.zh: 七國反書聞，天子乃遣太尉條侯周亞夫將三十六將軍往擊吳楚；
units.en: News of the seven kingdoms’ revolt reached court; the emperor sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu of Tiaohou with thirty-six generals against Wu and Chu;
units.literal: When word of the seven states' rebellion reached the throne, the Son of Heaven dispatched Grand Commandant Marquis of Tiaohou Zhou Yafu with thirty-six generals to strike Wu and Chu;

units.zh: 陛下多病志逸，不能省察。
units.en: The Son of Heaven is sick in body and distracted in will; he cannot see through the plot.
units.literal: The sovereign is often ill in mind and body and cannot look into these matters.

units.zh: 二月，吳王兵既破，敗走，於是天子制詔將軍：「蓋聞為善者天報以福，為非者天報以殃。
units.en: In the second month Wu’s army was shattered; the emperor told his generals: “Heaven crowns virtue with fortune and strikes evil with woe.
units.literal: In the second month the King of Wu's army had already been broken and fled in defeat; the Son of Heaven then issued an edict to the generals: “We have heard that Heaven rewards the good with blessing and the wicked with calamity.

units.zh: 王頓首膝行對曰：「今者，朝錯天子用事臣，變更高皇帝法令，侵奪諸侯地。
units.en: On his knees Ang said, “Chao Cuo rules the court, rewrites Gaozu’s statutes, and gnaws at princely fiefs.
units.literal: The king, knocking his head and crawling on his knees, replied, “At present Chao Cuo is the minister in charge at the Son of Heaven's side; he has altered the laws of the August Emperor Gaozu and seized the princes' lands.

units.zh: 又使使愬條侯於上，上使告條侯救梁，又守便宜不行。
units.en: They complained to the throne; the emperor told him to relieve Liang, yet he clung to his plan and stayed put.
units.literal: They also sent envoys to denounce Zhou Yafu to the emperor; the emperor ordered him to save Liang, yet he still held to tactical advantage and did not move.

units.zh: 及後使人為秋請，上復責問吳使者。
units.en: Later, when Wu sent an envoy for the autumn audience, the emperor again questioned and rebuked him.
units.literal: Later, when Wu sent a man for the autumn audience, the emperor again questioned and rebuked the Wu envoy.

units.zh: 於是天子皆赦吳使者歸之，而賜吳王几杖，老，不朝。
units.en: The Son of Heaven pardoned the envoys and sent them back, then gave the king of Wu a folding stool and staff in token of old age, freeing him from court calls.
units.literal: The emperor pardoned Wu’s envoys and sent them home, then bestowed on the king of Wu an arm-rest and staff as tokens of age, exempting him from court attendance.

units.zh: 遣曲周侯酈寄擊趙，將軍欒布擊齊，大將軍竇嬰屯滎陽監齊趙兵。
units.en: he sent Li Ji, marquis of Quzhou, against Zhao and Luan Bu against Qi, while Grand General Dou Ying encamped at Xingyang to keep watch over the armies of Qi and Zhao.
units.literal: he sent Marquis Li Ji of Quzhou against Zhao and General Luan Bu against Qi; Grand General Dou Ying encamped at Xingyang to keep watch over the Qi and Zhao armies.

units.zh: 上從其議，遂斬錯。
units.en: The emperor accepted his counsel and had Chao Cuo executed.
units.literal: The emperor accepted his counsel and had Chao Cuo executed.

units.zh: 高皇帝親垂功德，建立諸侯，幽王、悼惠王絕無後，孝文皇帝哀憐加惠，王幽王子遂，悼惠王子卬等，令奉其先王宗廟，為漢藩國，德配天地，明並日月。
units.en: Gaozu established the kingdoms. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off, Emperor Wen compassionately made You’s son Sui, Daohui’s son Ang, and others kings so that they could tend their forefathers’ shrines and serve as Han’s outer bulwarks. His virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.
units.literal: The August Emperor Gaozu personally bestowed merit and virtue by establishing the princes. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off without successors, Emperor Xiaowen took pity and extended his grace, making King You's son Sui, King Daohui's son Ang, and others kings so that they could maintain their forefathers' ancestral temples and serve as Han's outer bulwarks—his virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.

units.zh: 而吳王濞背德反義，誘受天下亡命罪人，亂天下幣，稱疾不朝二十餘年。
units.en: Yet Liu Bi spurned virtue, drew in fugitives, disrupted the currency, and for more than twenty years pleaded illness and stayed away from court.
units.literal: Yet the King of Wu Liu Bi turned his back on virtue and violated righteousness, enticed and harbored fugitive criminals from the realm, threw the realm's currency into confusion, and for more than twenty years claimed illness and did not attend court.

units.zh: 有司數請濞罪，孝文皇帝寬之，欲其改行為善。
units.en: Officials begged his head; Wendi spared him, hoping he would mend his ways.
