units.literal: The authorities repeatedly requested Bi's punishment; Emperor Xiaowen was lenient and wished him to change his conduct for the good.

units.zh: 今乃與楚王戊、趙王遂、膠西王卬、濟南王辟光、菑川王賢、膠東王雄渠約從謀反，為逆無道，起兵以危宗廟，賊殺大臣及漢使者，迫劫萬民，伐殺無罪，燒殘民家，掘其丘壟，甚為虐暴。
units.en: Now he has allied with Liu Wu of Chu, Liu Sui of Zhao, Liu Ang of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang of Jinan, Liu Xian of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong to plot rebellion. These lawless traitors menace the temples, murder ministers and envoys, coerce the people, kill the innocent, burn their homes, and dig open their graves. Their cruelty is monstrous.
units.literal: Now he has joined with Liu Wu, king of Chu, Liu Sui, king of Zhao, Liu Ang, king of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang, king of Jinan, Liu Xian, king of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu, king of Jiaodong, in an alliance to plot rebellion. Lawless in their treason, they raised troops to endanger the ancestral temples, murdered great ministers and Han envoys, coerced the people, slaughtered the innocent, burned commoners' homes, and dug open their tombs—utterly cruel and violent.

units.zh: 而卬等又重逆無道，燒宗廟，鹵御物，朕甚痛之。
units.en: Ang’s crew have burned the shrines and plundered the palace stores—Our heart is torn.
units.literal: Yet Ang and the others have again been utterly lawless, burned the temples, looted the imperial gear—the pain of this is great in Us.

units.zh: 朕素服避正殿，將軍其勸士大夫擊反虜。
units.en: We wear mourning and quit the main hall—generals, drive your men at the traitors.
units.literal: We have donned plain dress and avoided the main hall; generals, urge your officers to strike the rebels.

units.zh: 擊反虜者，深入多殺為功，斬首捕虜比三百石以上皆殺，無有所置。
units.en: Advance deep and kill many to earn merit; execute every captured rebel of three-hundred-picul rank or higher, sparing none.
units.literal: Those who strike the rebels shall take deep advances and heavy killing as merit; every captured rebel of the three-hundred-picul rank or above shall be put to death, with none spared.

units.zh: 敢有議詔及不如詔者，皆要斬。」
units.en: Debate the decree or disobey it—death by waist chop.”
units.literal: Whoever dares debate the edict or fail to match the edict—waist cut in two.”

units.zh: 夫能詘於一人之下，而信於萬乘之上者，湯武是也。
units.en: Tang and King Wu could submit to one ruler for a time and ultimately rise above the sovereign of ten thousand chariots.
units.literal: Those able to bend beneath one man and then rise above the ruler of ten thousand chariots were Tang and King Wu.

units.zh: 至若北道姚氏，西道諸杜，南道仇景，東道趙佗羽公子，南陽趙調之徒，盜跖而居民間者耳，曷足道哉！
units.en: As for the Yao gang on the northern road, the Du clans on the western, Qiu Jing in the south, the so-called Zhao Tuo princeling in the east, Zhao Diao in Nanyang—they were bandits in broad daylight, hardly worth ink.
units.literal: As for the Yao clan of the northern road, the various Du of the western road, Qiu Jing of the southern road, Zhao Tuoyu, courtesy Gongzi, of the eastern road, Zhao Diao of Nanyang, and their sort, they were mere Robber Zhis living among the people. How are they worth speaking of?

units.zh: 放勛、重華之世，咸無意於受終，當塗、典午之君，雖有心於揖讓，皆以英才處萬乘，高勳御四海，故能大庇黔首，光宅區縣。
units.en: Yao and Shun took the throne without seeking it; the rulers of Wei and Jin, though they spoke of abdication, still set men of rare talent upon the throne and men of towering merit at the helm of the realm—thus they sheltered the people and brought order to the land.
units.literal: In the ages of Fangxun and Chonghua, both were without intent to receive the end; the lords of Dangtu and Dianwu, though they had mind for yielding, all alike placed men of outstanding talent upon the ten-thousand chariots, with high merit steering the four seas—therefore they could greatly shelter the black-haired people and brightly settle the districts and counties.

units.zh: 既而煙雲表色，日月呈瑞，緯聚東井，龍見譙邦，除舊布新，既彰玄象，遷虞事夏，且協謳訟，[2]九域八荒，同布衷款，百神群祀，皆有誠願。
units.en: Then clouds and mist took auspicious hues; sun and moon showed signs; stars clustered at the Eastern Well; a dragon was seen in Qiao. The old order gave way to the new, and Heaven's signs were plain; as in the transfer from Shun to Yu, the people's acclaim agreed. [2] Within the nine provinces and beyond the eight directions, loyal petitions poured in; every spirit and rite was offered in earnest devotion.
units.literal: Thereafter clouds and mist showed color; sun and moon presented omens; constellations gathered at the Eastern Well; a dragon appeared in the Qiao region. Removing the old and spreading the new, the dark signs were already manifest; shifting from Yu and serving Xia, and moreover matching the songs of praise, [2] the nine domains and eight wilds alike spread forth sincere petitions; the hundred spirits and assembled sacrifices all had sincere wish.

units.zh: 梁氏以天祿斯改，期運永終，欽若唐、虞，推其鼎玉，朕東西退讓，拜手陳辭，避舜子於箕山之陽，求支伯於滄洲之野，而公卿敦逼，率土翹惶，天命難稽，遂享嘉祚。
units.en: The House of Liang, its mandate spent, its turn complete—like Tang and Yu they offered up the regalia. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and pleaded our case, hiding like Shun's son on Mount Ji's sunny slope, seeking Zhibo on Cangzhou's wilds—but ministers pressed us and the realm looked up in dread. Heaven's mandate would not wait; thus We received the glorious throne.
units.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing now changed, its allotted span ended forever—reverently in accord with Tang and Yu, they pushed forth their tripod and jade. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and spoke our plea, avoiding Shun's son on the sunny slope of Mount Ji, seeking Zhibo on the wilds of Cangzhou—but the dukes and ministers pressed urgently; the whole land looked up in alarm. Heaven's mandate could not be delayed; thus We received the fine fortune.

units.zh: 時穆子容為巡省使，嘆曰：「古人有言：『聞伯夷之風，貪夫廉，懦夫有立。』
units.en: At the time Mu Zirong was touring inspector; he sighed and said, "The ancients said: 'Hear the wind of Bo Yi, and the greedy grow honest; the timid stand firm.'
units.literal: At the time Mu Zirong was touring inspector; he sighed and said: "The ancients had a saying: 'When one hears the wind of Bo Yi, the greedy grow honest and the timid stand firm.'

units.zh: 李渾 子湛 渾弟繪 族子公緒 李璵 弟瑾 族弟曉 鄭述祖 子元德
units.en: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande
units.literal: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande

units.zh: 昔豫子吞炭壞形以奉見異，齊客隕首公門以報恩施，知氏、孟嘗猶有死士，何況將軍之門！」
units.en: Yurang disfigured himself with charcoal for his lord; a Qi retainer dashed out his brains at the gate to repay a kindness. Even the houses of Zhi Bo and Lord Mengchang kept men willing to die—how much more may your own gate command such loyalty!"
units.literal: Anciently Yuzi swallowed charcoal and ruined form to serve and show strangeness; a Qi guest dashed out brains at the ducal gate to repay grace shown; the Zhi clan and Lord Mengchang still had death-sworn men—how much more the general's gate!"

units.zh: 公孫弘以宰相，布被，食不重味，為下先，然而無益於俗，稍務於功利矣。
units.en: Even under Gongsun Hong's austere personal style, court policy kept drifting toward utilitarian gain.
units.literal: With Gongsun Hong as chancellor, though he wore plain cloth and ate simply as example, he did not improve social custom; policy increasingly turned to utility and profit.

units.zh: 自孫弘以春秋之義繩臣下取漢相，張湯以峻文決理為廷尉，於是見知之法生，而廢格沮誹窮治之獄用矣。
units.en: Moralist and legalist techniques fused into a harsher prosecutorial regime, including broad guilt-by-knowledge doctrines.
units.literal: From Sun Hong using Spring and Autumn standards to bind ministers and become Han chancellor, and Zhang Tang using severe textual law as chief justice, then laws of 'seen and known' arose, and prosecutions for obstruction, disparagement, and exhaustive investigation were used.

units.zh: 以中大夫令免為車騎將軍屯飛狐，故楚相蘇意為將軍屯句注，將軍張武屯北地，河內太守周亞夫為將軍次細柳，宗正劉禮為將軍次霸上，祝茲侯徐厲為將軍次棘門，以備胡。
units.en: He appointed Court Gentleman Ling Mian as Chariot and Cavalry General stationed at Feihu Pass, former Chu Chancellor Su Yi as general stationed at Gouzhu Pass, General Zhang Wu stationed at Beidi, Hedong Governor Zhou Yafu as general stationed at Xiliu, Imperial Kinsman Liu Li as general stationed at Bashang, and Marquis Xu Li of Zhuzi as general stationed at Jimen, all to defend against the Xiongnu.
units.literal: He appointed Court Gentleman Ling Mian as Chariot and Cavalry General stationed at Feihu, former Chu Chancellor Su Yi as general stationed at Gouzhu, General Zhang Wu stationed at Beidi, Hedong Governor Zhou Yafu as general stationed at Xiliu, Imperial Kinsman Liu Li as general stationed at Bashang, and Marquis Xu Li of Zhuzi as general stationed at Jimen, to prepare against the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 令中尉亞夫為車騎將軍，屬國悍為將屯將軍，郎中令張武為復土將軍，發近縣卒萬六千人，發內史卒萬五千人，臧郭穿 復土屬將軍武。
units.en: He appointed Superintendent of the Capital Zhou Yafu as Chariot and Cavalry General, Protector of Dependent States Han as Garrison General, and Palace Assistant Zhang Wu as Restorer of Soil General. He mobilized 16,000 troops from nearby counties and 15,000 from the Capital District; excavating the outer burial enclosure and covering it with earth was assigned to General Wu.
units.literal: He commanded Superintendent of the Capital Zhou Yafu to be Chariot and Cavalry General, Protector of the Dependent States Han to be Garrison General, Palace Assistant Zhang Wu to be Restorer of Soil General, mobilizing 16,000 troops from nearby counties and 15,000 troops from the Capital District; excavating the outer burial enclosure and covering it with earth was assigned to General Wu.

units.zh: 伏聞朝議以高祖大造區夏，道侔姬文，提記明堂，式配上帝。
units.en: We hear the court argues that because the High Ancestor shaped the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, he raised the Bright Hall to sacrifice to the Lord on High.
units.literal: We have heard that court discussion, because the High Ancestor greatly fashioned the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, raised the record of the Bright Hall to match the Lord on High.

units.zh: 對曰：「數尋伊、霍之傳，不讀曹、馬之書。」
units.en: He replied, "I pore over the lives of Yi Yin and Huo Guang — not the chronicles of Cao Cao and the Sima clan."
units.literal: He replied: "I often seek the biographies of Yi Yin and Huo Guang; I do not read the books of Cao [Cao] and the Sima [clan]."

units.zh: 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶
units.en: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao
units.literal: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao

units.zh: 莊蹻起，楚分而為四參。
units.en: Zhuang Qiao arose, and Chu was divided into four portions.
units.literal: Zhuang Qiao arose, Chu divided became four portions.

units.zh: 譬若以周、邵為丞相，孔丘為御史大夫，太公為將軍，畢公高拾遺於後，弁嚴子為衛尉，皋陶為大理，後稷為司農，伊尹為少府，子贛使外國，顏、閔為博士，子夏為太常，益為右扶風，季路為執金吾，契為鴻臚，龍逢為宗正，伯夷為京兆，管仲為馮翊，魯般為將作，仲山甫為光祿，申伯為太僕，延陵季子為水衡，百里奚為典屬國，柳下惠為大長秋，史魚為司直，蘧伯玉為太傅，孔父為詹事，孫叔敖為諸侯相，子產為郡守，王慶忌為期門，夏育為鼎官，羿為旄頭，宋萬為式道候。」
units.en: Imagine the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao as your chancellors; Confucius as chief censor; the Grand Duke as commander; Duke Bi Gao as court remonstrant; Bian Zhuangzi as captain of the guard; Gao Yao as chief judge; Hou Ji as minister of agriculture; Yi Yin as palace treasurer; Zigong as foreign envoy; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian as court scholars; Zixia as master of rites; Yi as western capital intendant; Zilu as capital commandant; Xie as master of guest ceremonies; Guan Longpeng as keeper of the imperial genealogy; the minister Boyi as metropolitan governor; Guan Zhong as northern capital intendant; Lu Ban as chief engineer; Zhong Shanfu as palace chamberlain; the Earl of Shen as master of the horse; Prince Jizi of Yanling as keeper of parks and waters; Baili Xi as commissioner for dependent peoples; Liuxia Hui as chamberlain to the empress; Shi Yu as censor of conduct; Qu Boyu as grand tutor; Kong Fu as supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao as chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan as commandery governor; Prince Qingji as a palace gate guard; Xia Yu as cauldron officer; Yi the Archer as vanguard officer; and Song Wan as road-clearing scout."
units.literal: It is as if you had made the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao your chancellors; Confucius your Censor-in-Chief; the Grand Duke your general; Duke Bi Gao your remonstrant at the rear; Bian Zhuangzi your Commandant of the Guards; Gao Yao your Chief Justice; Hou Ji your Minister of Agriculture; Yi Yin your Privy Treasurer; Zigong your envoy abroad; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian your Erudites; Zixia your Minister of Ceremonies; Yi your western capital intendant; Zilu your Capital Commandant; Xie your Grand Herald; Guan Longpeng your Director of the Imperial Clan; the minister Boyi your Metropolitan Governor; Guan Zhong your northern capital intendant; Lu Ban your Superintendent of Works; Zhong Shanfu your Chamberlain for Attendants; the Earl of Shen your Grand Coachman; Prince Jizi of Yanling your Superintendent of Waters and Parks; Baili Xi your Director of Dependent States; Liuxia Hui your Chamberlain for the Empress; Shi Yu your Rectifier; Qu Boyu your Grand Tutor; Kong Fu your supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao your chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan your commandery governor; Prince Qingji your Palace Gate Guard; Xia Yu your Cauldron Officer; Yi the Archer your Vanguard Officer; and Song Wan your road-clearing scout."

units.zh: 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為其父作佳傳，收論尒朱榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。
units.en: Wenlüe once paid Wei Shou heavily to glorify his father in print—hence Shou’s likening of Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang.
units.literal: Wenlüe once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold and asked him to write a fine biography of his father; that Wei Shou compared Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang was largely for this reason.

units.zh: 乃髡鉗布，衣褐，置廣柳車中，并與其家僮數十人，之魯朱家所賣之。
units.en: They shaved his head, clamped him in the convict's collar, dressed him in a laborer's hemp, stowed him in a funeral cart with several dozen household servants, and drove him to Zhu Jia of Lu to be sold off as a slave.
units.literal: Thereupon they shaved his head and put the iron collar on Bu, clothed him in coarse cloth, placed him in a broad-willow cart, together with several tens of his household slaves, and went to the place of Zhu Jia of Lu to sell him.

units.zh: 朱家心知其季布也，買置田舍。
units.en: Zhu Jia recognized him at once as Ji Bu, bought him, and lodged him on a country estate.
units.literal: Zhu Jia in his heart knew he was Ji Bu; he bought him and placed him in a field house.

units.zh: 滕公心知朱家大俠，意布匿其所，乃許諾。
units.en: Xiahou Ying knew Zhu Jia for a famous man of chivalry and guessed Ji Bu lay hidden with him; he agreed to speak.
units.literal: Lord Teng in his heart knew Zhu Jia was a great knight-errant; he suspected Bu was hidden at his place; thereupon he promised.

units.zh: 侍間，果言如朱家指。
units.en: When a suitable occasion came, he repeated Zhu Jia's argument to the throne.
units.literal: Waiting for an interval, he indeed spoke as Zhu Jia had indicated.

units.zh: 當是時，諸公皆多布能摧剛為柔，朱家亦以此名聞當世。
units.en: Men of rank admired Ji Bu for bending unyielding pride into survival, and Zhu Jia's name rang through the age for it.
units.literal: At this time, the various lords all praised Bu for being able to break hardness and make softness; Zhu Jia also by this had his name heard in that age.

units.zh: 項籍滅，高祖購求布千金，敢有舍匿，罪三族。
units.en: After Xiang Yu fell, Gaozu posted a reward of a thousand pounds of gold for Ji Bu, with death for three generations of kin for anyone who dared hide him.
units.literal: When Xiang Ji was destroyed, Gaozu offered a thousand catties of gold for Ji Bu; whoever dared shelter or conceal him would suffer punishment extending to three kin groups.

units.zh: 乃之雒陽見汝陰侯滕公，說曰：「季布何罪？
units.en: Then he traveled to Luoyang to see Xiahou Ying, the Marquis of Ru-yin, and argued, "What wrong has Ji Bu done?
units.literal: Thereupon he went to Luoyang to see the Marquis of Ru-yin, Lord Teng, and urged him, saying, "What crime has Ji Bu committed?

units.zh: 臣各為其主用，職耳。
units.en: Ministers serve their own lords—that is simply what duty requires.
units.literal: Ministers each for their lord are employed; it is duty only.

units.zh: 項氏臣豈可盡誅邪？
units.en: Are we to execute every man who once served the house of Xiang?
units.literal: The Xiang clan's ministers—how can they all be executed?

units.zh: 今上始得天下，而以私怨求一人，何示不廣也！
units.en: The Son of Heaven has only just won the realm; to hound one man out of personal spite shows a narrowness ill befitting his position.
units.literal: Now the sovereign has just obtained the empire, yet by private resentment seeks one man—what a narrow show this makes!

units.zh: 且以季布之賢，漢求之急如此，此不北走胡，南走越耳。
units.en: A man of Ji Bu's caliber, pressed this hard, will flee north to the Xiongnu or south to Nanyue.
units.literal: Moreover, by Ji Bu's worthiness, the Han's search for him being so urgent—this is nothing but fleeing north to the Hu or fleeing south to Yue.

units.zh: 夫忌壯士以資敵國，此伍子胥所以鞭荊平之墓也。
units.en: To drive a brave man into the arms of a rival is the sort of blunder that made Wu Zixu flog the grave of King Ping of Chu.
units.literal: As for driving away a brave man so as to aid an enemy state—this is why Wu Zixu whipped the tomb of King Ping of Chu.

units.zh: 君何不從容為上言之？」
units.en: Why not find a tactful moment and put this to the emperor yourself?"
units.literal: Why do you not speak of this to the sovereign at your leisure?"

units.zh: 至雒陽，見劇孟，喜曰：「
units.en: When he reached Luoyang and saw Ju Meng, he said with delight, “
units.literal: When he reached Luoyang and saw Ju Meng, he said with delight, “

units.zh: 又以為諸侯已得劇孟。
units.en: I feared the rebels had already won Ju Meng over.
units.literal: I had also thought the princes had already secured Ju Meng.

units.zh: 孟今無動，吾據滎陽，滎陽以東無足憂者。」
units.en: Since he has not stirred, Xingyang is mine, and east of it we have little to fear.”
units.literal: Now that Meng has not stirred, I hold Xingyang, and east of Xingyang there is nothing to worry about.”

units.zh: 季布，楚人也，為任俠有名。
units.en: Ji Bu was a native of Chu who had won renown as a knight-errant.
units.literal: Ji Bu was a man of Chu; as a knight-errant he had a reputation.

units.zh: 布聞，寄書諫長君曰：「吾聞曹丘生非長者，勿與通。」
units.en: When Ji Bu heard of it, he wrote to Dou Changjun warning him, "Cao Qiusheng is no man of substance; have nothing to do with him."
units.literal: Ji Bu heard of this and sent a letter admonishing Dou Changjun: "I have heard that Cao Qiusheng is not a venerable elder; do not associate with him."

units.zh: 曹丘至，則揖布曰：「楚人諺曰『得黃金百，不如得季布諾』，足下何以得此聲梁楚之間哉？
units.en: When Cao arrived, he bowed to Ji Bu and said, "Chu has a saying: 'A hundred pounds of gold cannot buy Ji Bu's word'—how did you earn such fame across Liang and Chu?
units.literal: When Cao Qiu arrived, then he bowed to Bu and said, "The men of Chu have a proverb: 'Obtaining yellow gold a hundred is not as good as obtaining Ji Bu's promise'—how did you obtain this reputation between Liang and Chu?

units.zh: 布弟季心氣蓋關中，遇人恭謹，為任俠，方數千里，士爭為死。
units.en: Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin overshadowed all Guanzhong in sheer force of character; in person he was courteous and restrained, yet as a knight-errant his reputation ran for a thousand miles, and fighting men vied to die for him.
units.literal: Bu's younger brother Ji Xin, spirit covering Guanzhong, meeting people was respectful and careful; as knight-errant, square several thousand li, gentlemen strove to die for him.

units.zh: 當是時，季心以勇，布以諾，聞關中。
units.en: In those days Guanzhong knew Ji Xin for his courage and Ji Bu for keeping his word.
units.literal: At this time, Ji Xin by bravery, Bu by promise, were heard of in Guanzhong.

units.zh: 布母弟丁公，為項羽將，逐窘高祖彭城西。
units.en: Ji Bu's maternal uncle Ding Gong, a general under Xiang Yu, had pressed Gaozu hard west of Pengcheng.
units.literal: Ji Bu's maternal uncle Ding Gong, being Xiang Yu's general, pursued and cornered Gaozu west of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 贊曰：以項羽之氣，而季布以勇顯名楚，身履軍搴旗者數矣，可謂壯士。
units.en: The historian's verdict: In an age dominated by Xiang Yu's fury, Ji Bu won fame in Chu for raw courage; he repeatedly charged into battle and tore enemy banners from their poles—a true fighting man.
units.literal: The appraisal says: By Xiang Yu's fierce spirit, yet Ji Bu by bravery displayed name in Chu; personally in the army seizing banners—several times—can be called a brave warrior.

units.zh: 竇長君曰：「季將軍不說足下，足下無往。」
units.en: Dou Changjun said, "General Ji dislikes you; you had better not go."
units.literal: Dou Changjun said, "General Ji is not pleased with you; you must not go."

units.zh: 項籍使將兵，數窘漢王。
units.en: Xiang Yu put him in command of troops, and time and again he cornered the King of Han.
units.literal: Xiang Ji had him lead troops, and he repeatedly embarrassed the King of Han.

units.zh: 彼自負其材，受辱不羞，欲有所用其未足也，故終為漢名將。
units.en: He trusted his own abilities; shame did not break him because he still meant to put his gifts to use. In the end he became one of the Han's celebrated generals.
units.literal: He himself bore his talents; receiving humiliation he was not ashamed, wishing to have something to use of what was not yet sufficient; therefore in the end he became a Han famous general.

units.zh: 布召見，謝，拜郎中。
units.en: Ji Bu was summoned to court, thanked the emperor, and was appointed a gentleman of the palace.
units.literal: Bu was summoned and seen; he thanked; he was appointed gentleman of the palace.

units.zh: 孝惠時，為中郎將。
units.en: Under Emperor Hui he rose to general of the palace gentlemen.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaohui, he was general of the gentlemen of the palace.

units.zh: 布為河東守。
units.en: Ji Bu was appointed governor of Hedong.
units.literal: Bu was Hedong governor.

units.zh: 孝文時，人有言其賢，召欲以為御史大夫。
units.en: Under Emperor Wen, word of his talent reached the throne; he was summoned with a view to making him grandee secretary.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowen, someone spoke of his worthiness; he was summoned with the intention of making him grandee secretary.

units.zh: 上乃赦布。
units.en: The emperor then granted Ji Bu a full pardon.
units.literal: The sovereign thereupon pardoned Bu.

units.zh: 布曰：「樊噲可斬也。
units.en: Ji Bu said, "Fan Kuai deserves execution.
units.literal: Bu said, "Fan Kuai can be beheaded.

units.zh: 夫以高帝兵三十餘萬，困於平城，噲時亦在其中。
units.en: Gaozu himself led over three hundred thousand men and was trapped at Pingcheng—and Fan Kuai was in that army.
units.literal: As for by Gaozu's troops of more than three hundred thousand being trapped at Pingcheng, at that time Kuai also was within them.

units.zh: 今噲奈何以十萬眾橫行匈奴中，面謾！
units.en: How dare he now boast that a mere hundred thousand could ride roughshod over the Xiongnu? He is lying to your faces!
units.literal: Now how can Kuai with a hundred thousand men rampage through the middle of the Xiongnu—lying to your faces!

units.zh: 且秦以事胡，陳勝等起。
units.en: Moreover, the Qin empire crumbled in part because it exhausted itself on the northern frontier, and Chen Sheng rose in rebellion.
units.literal: Moreover, because Qin exhausted itself on affairs with the Hu, Chen Sheng and others rose in rebellion.

units.zh: 今瘡痍未瘳，噲又面諛，欲搖動天下。」
units.en: The realm is still bleeding from those wars, and Fan Kuai flatters you to your face and would unsettle the whole empire again."
units.literal: Now the wounds are not yet healed, and Kuai again to the face flatters, wishing to shake and move the empire."

units.zh: 布進曰：「臣待罪河東，陛下無故召臣，此人必有以臣欺陛下者。
units.en: Ji Bu stepped forward and said, "I stand under sentence of fault at Hedong; Your Majesty summoned me without cause—someone must have oversold me to you.
units.literal: Bu advanced and said, "Your servant awaits punishment at Hedong; Your Majesty without reason summoned your servant—this person must have had something by which to deceive Your Majesty regarding your servant.

units.zh: 今臣至，無所受事，罷去，此人必有毀臣者。
units.en: Now that I am here, I am given no charge and dismissed—someone has blackened me behind my back.
units.literal: Now your servant has arrived, without receiving any charge, dismissed and sent away—someone must have slandered your servant.

units.zh: 夫陛下以一人譽召臣，一人毀去臣，臣恐天下有識者聞之，有以窺陛下。」
units.en: If one man's praise brings me to court and one man's slander sends me packing, thoughtful men everywhere will draw their own conclusions about Your Majesty's judgment."
units.literal: As for Your Majesty by one man's praise summoning your servant, by one man's slander sending away your servant—your servant fears the empire's knowing ones hearing it will have means to peer into Your Majesty."

units.zh: 及至困厄奴僇，苟活而不變，何也？
units.en: Yet when he was broken, enslaved, and humiliated, he clung to life without yielding his purpose—why was that?
units.literal: When it came to straits and humiliation as a slave, living ignobly yet not changing—why?

units.zh: 及楚相春申君亦見王無子，心利楚國，即獻有身妻而產懷王。
units.en: Chu's chancellor Lord Chunshen did the same when he saw the king had no heir, scheming for Chu's advantage by presenting a pregnant wife who bore King Huai of Chu.
units.literal: And Chu chancellor Lord Chunshen likewise saw the king had no son, his heart set on benefiting the state of Chu; he then presented a pregnant wife and she bore King Huai.

units.zh: 以如意擊幾自樂，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫、原憲焉。
units.en: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
units.literal: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

units.zh: 郭解，河內軹人也，溫善相人許負外孫也。
units.en: Guo Xie of Zhi in Henei was the maternal grandson of Xu Fu, the famous face-reader from Wen.
units.literal: Guo Xie was a man of Zhi in Henei, maternal grandson of the physiognomist Xu Fu of Wen.

units.zh: 盎曰：「劇孟雖博徒，然母死，客送葬車千餘乘，此亦有過人者。
units.en: Ang replied, 'Though Ju Meng is a gambler, when his mother died, over a thousand carriages of guests attended the funeral. A man who commands such loyalty has qualities that surpass the ordinary.
units.literal: Ang said: 'Though Ju Meng is a gambler, when his mother died, more than a thousand carriages of guests attended the funeral procession. This shows he has qualities that surpass those of ordinary men.

units.zh: 然關中長安樊中子，槐裡趙王孫，長陵高公子，西河郭翁中，太原魯翁孺，臨淮兒長卿，東陽陳君孺，雖為俠而恂恂有退讓君子之風。
units.en: Still, men like Fan Zhongzi in Chang'an, Zhao Wangsun in Huaili, Gao Gongzi in Changling, Guo Wengzhong of Xihe, Lu Wengru in Taiyuan, Er Changqing in Linhuai, and Chen Junru in Dongyang wore the knight's label yet behaved with courteous restraint.
units.literal: Yet within the pass—Fan Zhongzi of Chang'an, Zhao Wangsun of Huaili, Gao Gongzi of Changling, Guo Wengzhong of Xihe, Lu Wengru of Taiyuan, Er Changqing of Linhuai, Chen Junru of Dongyang—though they were knights, they were modest and had the bearing of gentlemen who yield.

units.zh: 自是之後，俠者極眾，而無足數者。
units.en: After that, bravos swarmed the empire, but few worth naming.
units.literal: From this time onward, those who were knights were extremely many, yet none worth counting.

units.zh: 累既攀夫傅說兮，奚不信而遂行？
units.en: Once you had climbed to Fu Yue in dream— why not trust the sign and press on?
units.literal: You had already climbed to Fu Yue— why not trust and go straight on?

units.zh: 楚田仲以俠聞，父事硃家，自以為行弗及也。
units.en: Tian Zhong of Chu, famed as a knight, treated Zhu Jia like a father and admitted he could not match him.
units.literal: Tian Zhong of Chu was known by knight-errantry; serving Zhu Jia with a father's deference, he considered his own conduct not equal.

units.zh: 田仲死後，有劇孟。
units.en: After Tian Zhong died, Ju Meng came to the fore.
units.literal: After Tian Zhong died, there was Ju Meng.

units.zh: 外戚大臣魏其、武安之屬競逐於京師，布衣遊俠劇孟、郭解之徒馳騖於閭閻，權行州域，力折公侯。
units.en: Inside Chang'an the Dou and Tian factions jostled for power, while in the alleys bare-chested swordsmen like Ju Meng and Guo Xie built reputations that cowed nobles and bent whole commanderies.
units.literal: Affinal ministers such as Marquis Weiqi and Marquis Wu'an vied in pursuit at the capital; common-cloth wandering knights such as Ju Meng and Guo Xie raced in the lanes—their authority ran through provinces, their force bent marquises and dukes.

units.zh: 解為人靜悍，不飲酒。
units.en: Guo Xie was soft-spoken and deadly sober.
units.literal: Xie as a person was quiet and fierce, and did not drink wine.

units.zh: 解父任俠，孝文時誅死。
units.en: His father had lived by the sword and died on the execution ground under Emperor Wen.
units.literal: Xie's father practiced knight-errantry; in Emperor Xiaowen's time he was executed to death.

units.zh: 少時陰賊感概，不快意，所殺甚眾。
units.en: As a youth he nursed grudges in silence and left a long trail of corpses whenever he felt slighted.
units.literal: In youth he was secretly vicious and stirred by indignation; when displeased, those he killed were very many.

units.zh: 以軀借友報仇，臧命作奸剽攻，休乃鑄錢掘塚，不可勝數。
units.en: He lent his blade for friends' feuds, hid wanted men, led raids, and in quieter moments counterfeited cash and robbed graves—too often to count.
units.literal: Lending his body to friends to avenge wrongs, harboring fugitives, doing wickedness, raiding and attacking; in leisure then casting coin and digging tombs—beyond counting.

units.zh: 適有天幸，窘急常得脫，若遇赦。
units.en: Heaven smiled on him: every tight corner opened like a general pardon.
units.literal: He happened to have heaven's luck; in straits and urgency he constantly got away, as if meeting an amnesty.

units.zh: 況於郭解之倫，以匹夫之細，竊殺生之權，其罪已不容於誅矣。
units.en: How much less pardonable are commoners like Guo Xie who arrogate the power of life and death—no punishment could be enough.
units.literal: How much more men like Guo Xie, by the meanness of a common fellow, usurping the power over life and death—their guilt already brooked no room within execution.

units.zh: 觀其溫良泛愛，振窮周急，謙退不伐，亦皆有絕異之姿。
units.en: Yet watch them help the poor, soothe the desperate, and refuse praise—they could show a charisma few gentlemen matched.
units.literal: Observing their warmth and goodness, broad love, raising the destitute and relieving the urgent, modest retreat without boasting—they also all had surpassingly unusual bearing.

units.zh: 惜乎不入於道德，苟放縱於末流，殺身亡宗，非不幸也。
units.en: What a waste that they never steered that energy into true virtue, but rode the fad to ruin—death and lineage cut off were not accidents but the natural bill.
units.literal: It is regrettable that they did not enter into morality and virtue, but recklessly gave rein in the downstream current; killing the body and destroying the clan—this is not misfortune.

units.zh: 軹人楊季主子為縣掾，隔之，解兄子斷楊掾頭。
units.en: Yang Jizhu's son, a county clerk, blocked the convoy, so Guo Xie's elder brother's son took the man's head.
units.literal: A son of Yang Jizhu of Zhi was a county clerk and blocked him; Xie's elder brother's son cut off Clerk Yang's head.

units.zh: 邑人又殺楊季主，季主家上書人又殺闕下。
units.en: Locals murdered Yang Jizhu; when his kin sent a petitioner to the throne, someone cut the petitioner down on the palace steps.
units.literal: Townsmen again killed Yang Jizhu; Jizhu's family sent up a memorialist, and the memorialist was again killed below the palace gate.

units.zh: 而符離王孟，亦以俠稱江、淮之間。
units.en: Wang Meng of Fuli was another blade between the Yangzi and the Huai.
units.literal: Moreover Wang Meng of Fuli was also called a knight-errant between the Yangzi and Huai.

units.zh: 適趙，平原君側行撇席。
units.en: When he went to Zhao, Lord Pingyuan stepped aside and personally swept his mat in deference.
units.literal: When he went to Zhao, Lord Pingyuan sidestepped and swept aside his mat in deference.

units.zh: 對捍使者尚得死坐，況遊道吐不臣之言，犯慢上之罪，口稱夷、齊，心懷盜跖，欺公賣法，受納苞苴，產隨官厚，財與位積，雖贓汚未露，而姦詐如是。
units.en: Resisting an envoy earns death; how much more unministered words, slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harbors robbers, deceiving the public, taking bribes—wealth piled with rank though bribery was not yet exposed.
units.literal: Resisting an envoy still earns death; how much more Youdao's unministered words, the crime of slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harboring robbers, deceiving the public and selling the law, receiving wrapped bribes—property following office thick, wealth with rank piled; though bribery was not yet exposed, treachery was such.

units.zh: 昔晏平仲納延陵之誨，終免欒高之難；
units.en: Yan Ying heeded Yanling's warning and escaped the Luan-Gao purge;
units.literal: In the past Yan Pingzhong accepted Yanling's instruction and in the end escaped the disaster of Luan and Gao;
